Weitere Informationen über Center for Law & Economics sowie zum SNF-Projekt , finden Sie auf den folgenden Webseiten: Center for Law & Economics und SNF-Projekt . Für Auskünfte steht Ihnen Dr. Jakob Merane, (jmerane@ethz.ch) (keine Bewerbungsunterlagen), gerne zur Verfügung.

Die Doktorandenstelle ist an der Professur von Prof. Alexander Stremitzer angesiedelt.

Dottorando/a in Giurisprudenza 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato --- descrizione As part of the SNSF-funded project „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary, we are working together with Swiss courts to investigate how artificial intelligence can be responsibly integrated into justice. Project background The PhD student body is responsible for the empirical research of AI-based decision-making aids in the judiciary. The doctoral student will investigate the effects of such systems on judicial practice – through the design and implementation of field experiments in cooperation with Swiss courts and their legal and institutional evaluation. --- Mansioni - Investigation of judicial decision-making processes and legal argumentation in interaction with AI tools - Participation in the development of experimental design and evaluation frameworks for AI-based decision-making - Cooperation with the technical team to investigate the interaction between AI systems and legal users - Publication of research results in leading journals and presentation at international conferences - The body is conceived as a cumulative dissertation at the interface of law, computer science and empirical social science - Our offices are located in Zurich city centre - The working languages are German and English.
• Requisiti - Bring an excellent Bachelor and Master's degree in Law from a German-speaking university (Germany, Austria or Switzerland) - A strong interest in the impact of AI on law and society - Bringing interest in field experiments and experimental research designs - The willingness to learn and apply quantitative and empirical research methods - have very good English skills; German and French skills are advantageous --- Luogo di lavoro

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Vehicle Sensor and Remote Sensing Analysis for Road Safety

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Enviromental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student. This position focuses on leveraging vehicle sensors, remote sensing, and machine learning to support modern urban road safety analysis as a part of a larger EU project.

Project background

The new EU Horizon project advances safe active mobility uptake and research by introducing a human-centred, evidence-based approach that integrates actual and perceived safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and micromobility users. Moving beyond conventional crash-focused approaches, it captures near-misses, dynamic interactions, and embodied safety experiences that shape behaviour and mode choice. The project combines multi-source traffic, infrastructure, vehicle, and health data with immersive eXtended Reality (XR) experimentation and explainable Artificial Intelligence to analyse safety-critical situations that are rare, underreported, or ethically impossible to observe in real traffic. Explainable AI ensures transparency and interpretability, supporting trust, transferability, and policy relevance. The project translates these insights into harmonised assessment methodologies, predictive models, and validated indicators, enabling robust evaluation and comparison of regulatory, infrastructural, technological, and behavioural interventions across Safe System Approach stakeholders. Special focus is placed on interactions between users with differing masses and speeds, including e-bikes, e-cargo bikes, and e-scooters, for both personal mobility and urban logistics. Large-scale pilots in four European cities validate methods in real traffic, support cross-city learning, and ensure applicability under diverse safety, infrastructure and cultural conditions. Implemented by a multidisciplinary consortium bridging engineering, behavioural science, XR, AI, urban planning, and policy, the project delivers actionable, standardised guidance that accelerates safer, more inclusive active and micromobility systems across Europe.

Planning safe urban transport systems is inherently complex: interventions last for decades, require significant investment, must fit within constrained spaces, and must satisfy ever-changing user needs. Modern data collection methods - such as high-frequency on-board vehicle sensors and computer-vision imagery - are well-suited to capture these complexities via near real-time, high-resolution insights. However, collecting, processing, and operationalizing these big data volumes is a challenge due to heterogeneous data structures and heavy computational demands.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state-of-the-art in sensor and remote sensing data fusion for urban transport infrastructure safety analysis. The candidate will develop new tools and methods that integrate big data, computer vision, and machine learning. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Develop a Scalable Sensing Pipeline: Design and implement a software/tool architecture capable of processing multi-source vehicle sensor, camera, and remote sensing data streams

• Automate Feature & Factor Identification: Train machine learning and computer vision models within the pipeline to automatically detect built-environment infrastructure characteristics and related factors affecting micromobility safety and comfort

• Generate Mapping & Diagnostic Outputs: Ensure the software accepts diverse inputs and generates structured, high-quality data outputs optimized for spatial mapping, risk diagnosis, and downstream predictive safety modelling

• Collaborate via Real-World Pilots: Validate and refine the pipeline using real-world data from the project’s pilot cities, working in close coope

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione del PhD nel sensore del veicolo e analisi di rilevamento remoto per la sicurezza stradale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Gestione delle Infrastrutture, guidata dal Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di Costruzione e Gestione delle Infrastrutture del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Enviromentale e Geomatica, ha un'apertura per uno studente di dottorato. Questa posizione si concentra sulla leva dei sensori del veicolo, il telerilevamento e l'apprendimento automatico per supportare l'analisi moderna della sicurezza stradale urbana come parte di un progetto UE più ampio. Sfondo del progetto Il nuovo progetto EU Horizon promuove l'assorbimento e la ricerca di una mobilità attiva sicura introducendo un approccio basato su prove umane che integra la sicurezza reale e percepita per pedoni, ciclisti e utenti di micromobilità. Passando oltre i convenzionali approcci focalizzati agli urti, cattura vicino-misses, interazioni dinamiche e esperienze di sicurezza incarnate che modellano il comportamento e la scelta della modalità. Il progetto combina il traffico multi-fonte, l'infrastruttura, il veicolo e i dati sanitari con la sperimentazione immersiva eXtended Reality (XR) e l'intelligenza artificiale spiegabile per analizzare situazioni di sicurezza-critical che sono rare, sottovalutate, o eticamente impossibili da osservare nel traffico reale. La Spiegabile AI garantisce trasparenza e interpretabilità, sostenendo fiducia, trasferibilità e rilevanza politica. Il progetto traduce queste intuizioni in metodologie di valutazione armonizzate, modelli predittivi e indicatori convalidati, consentendo una valutazione e un confronto robusti di interventi normativi, infrastrutturali, tecnologici e comportamentali tra gli stakeholder di Safe System Approach. Particolare attenzione è posta sulle interazioni tra utenti con diverse masse e velocità, tra cui e-bike, e-cargo bike, e-scooters, sia per la mobilità personale che per la logistica urbana. I piloti su larga scala in quattro città europee convalidano i metodi nel traffico reale, supportano l'apprendimento trasversale e garantiscono l'applicabilità in diverse condizioni di sicurezza, infrastruttura e cultura. Implementato da un'ingegneria multidisciplinare di collegamento consortile, scienza comportamentale, XR, AI, pianificazione urbana e politica, il progetto offre una guida attuabile e standardizzata che accelera sistemi attivi e di micromobilità più sicuri e inclusivi in tutta Europa. La pianificazione di sistemi di trasporto urbano sicuri è intrinsecamente complessa: gli interventi durano per decenni, richiedono un investimento significativo, devono adattarsi all'interno di spazi limitati, e devono soddisfare le esigenze degli utenti in continua evoluzione. I moderni metodi di raccolta dei dati - come i sensori di veicoli a bordo ad alta frequenza e le immagini di computer-visione - sono adatti per catturare queste complessità attraverso intuizioni in tempo reale, ad alta risoluzione. Tuttavia, la raccolta, l'elaborazione e la operativizzazione di questi grandi volumi di dati è una sfida a causa di strutture di dati eterogenee e pesanti richieste computazionali. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a far progredire lo stato dell'arte nella fusione dei dati del sensore e del telerilevamento per l'analisi della sicurezza delle infrastrutture di trasporto urbano. Il candidato svilupperà nuovi strumenti e metodi che integrano grandi dati, visione del computer e machine learning. I compiti principali del candidato includono:
• Sviluppare una Pipeline di rilevamento scalabile: progettare e implementare un'architettura software/tool in grado di elaborare sensori, telecamere e flussi di dati di telerilevamento
• Identificazione automatica delle caratteristiche e dei fattori: Modelli di apprendimento della macchina da treno e visione del computer all'interno della pipeline per rilevare automaticamente le caratteristiche dell'infrastruttura dell'ambiente costruito e i fattori correlati che influenzano la sicurezza e il comfort della micromobilità
• Genera mappatura e uscite diagnostiche: Assicurarsi che il software accetti diversi input e genera uscite di dati strutturate e di alta qualità ottimizzate per mappatura spaziale, diagnosi di rischio e modellazione di sicurezza predittiva a valle
• Collaborare tramite Real-World Pilots: convalidare e perfezionare la pipeline utilizzando i dati reali delle città pilota del progetto, lavorando in stretta coope

Adey im Institut für Bau- und Infrastrukturmanagement der Abteilung für Zivil-, Umwelt- und Geomatiktechnik hat eine Eröffnung für einen Doktoranden. Diese Position konzentriert sich auf die Verwendung von Fahrzeugsensoren, die Fernerkundung und das maschinelle Lernen, um die moderne städtische Verkehrssicherheitsanalyse im Rahmen eines größeren EU-Projekts zu unterstützen. Projekt Hintergrund Das neue EU-Horizont-Projekt fördert die sichere aktive Mobilitätsaufnahme und -forschung durch die Einführung eines menschenzentrierten, evidenzbasierten Ansatzes, der die tatsächliche und wahrgenommene Sicherheit für Fußgänger, Radfahrer und Mikromobilitätsnutzer integriert. Über konventionelle Crash-fokussierte Ansätze hinweg zu bewegen, erfasst sie Nah-Maßnahmen, dynamische Interaktionen und verkörperte Sicherheitserlebnisse, die Verhalten und Moduswahl prägen. Das Projekt kombiniert Mehrquellen-Verkehrs-, Infrastruktur-, Fahrzeug- und Gesundheitsdaten mit immersiven eXtended Reality (XR)-Experimenten und erklärbaren künstlichen Intelligenzen, um sicherheitskritische Situationen zu analysieren, die selten, unterreportiert oder ethisch unmöglich sind, im realen Verkehr zu beobachten. Poste de doctorat en analyse du capteur de véhicule et de la télédétection pour la sécurité routière 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée La chaire de gestion de l'infrastructure, dirigée par le professeur Bryan T. Adey à l'Institut de construction et de gestion de l'infrastructure du Département de génie civil, environnemental et géomatique, a une ouverture pour un doctorant. Cette position vise à tirer parti des capteurs de véhicules, de la télédétection et de l'apprentissage automatique pour soutenir l'analyse moderne de la sécurité routière urbaine dans le cadre d'un projet plus vaste de l'UE. Contexte du projet Le nouveau projet Horizon de l'UE favorise la mobilité active sûre et la recherche en introduisant une approche axée sur l'homme et fondée sur des données probantes qui intègre la sécurité réelle et perçue des piétons, des cyclistes et des utilisateurs de la micromobilité. Au-delà des approches conventionnelles axées sur les accidents, il capte les quasi-incidents, les interactions dynamiques et les expériences de sécurité incarnées qui façonnent le comportement et le choix du mode. Le projet combine des données multisources sur le trafic, l'infrastructure, les véhicules et la santé avec l'expérimentation immersive eXtended Reality (XR) et l'intelligence artificielle explicable pour analyser des situations critiques en matière de sécurité qui sont rares, sous-déclarées ou impossibles à observer sur le plan éthique dans le trafic réel. L'IA explicable assure la transparence et l'interprétation, appuyant la confiance, la transférabilité et la pertinence des politiques. Le projet traduit ces informations en méthodes d'évaluation harmonisées, en modèles de prévision et en indicateurs validés, permettant une évaluation et une comparaison solides des interventions réglementaires, infrastructurelles, technologiques et comportementales des parties prenantes à l'approche du système sûr. Une attention particulière est accordée aux interactions entre les utilisateurs avec des masses et des vitesses différentes, y compris les vélos électroniques, les vélos e-cargo et les e-cooters, pour la mobilité personnelle et la logistique urbaine. Des projets pilotes de grande envergure dans quatre villes européennes valident des méthodes de trafic réel, soutiennent l'apprentissage interurbain et garantissent leur applicabilité dans des conditions de sécurité, d'infrastructure et de culture diverses. Mis en œuvre par un consortium multidisciplinaire d'ingénierie, de science comportementale, de XR, d'IA, d'urbanisme et de politique, le projet fournit des orientations concrètes et standardisées qui accélèrent des systèmes actifs plus sûrs, plus inclusifs et de micromobilité dans toute l'Europe. La planification de systèmes de transport urbain sûrs est intrinsèquement complexe : les interventions durent des décennies, nécessitent des investissements importants, doivent s'adapter à des espaces restreints et doivent répondre à des besoins changeants des utilisateurs. Les méthodes modernes de collecte de données - telles que les capteurs de véhicules embarqués à haute fréquence et les images de vision par ordinateur - sont bien adaptées pour saisir ces complexités grâce à des aperçus à haute résolution en temps quasi réel. Cependant, la collecte, le traitement et l'opérationnalisation de ces volumes de mégadonnées sont un défi en raison de structures de données hétérogènes et de fortes demandes de calcul. Description de l'emploi Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de la technique en matière de fusion des données de détection et de télédétection pour l'analyse de la sécurité des infrastructures de transport urbain. Le candidat développera de nouveaux outils et méthodes qui intègrent les mégadonnées, la vision informatique et l'apprentissage automatique. Les principales tâches du candidat seront les suivantes :
• Développer un pipeline de détection évolutive : concevoir et mettre en œuvre une architecture logicielle/outil capable de traiter des flux de données multisources de capteurs, de caméras et de télédétection de véhicules
• Automatiser l'identification des caractéristiques et des facteurs: Train machine learning et les modèles de vision informatique dans le pipeline pour détecter automatiquement les caractéristiques de l'infrastructure bâtie et les facteurs connexes affectant la sécurité et le confort de la micromobilité
• Générer la cartographie et les sorties diagnostiques : s'assurer que le logiciel accepte divers intrants et génère des sorties de données structurées et de haute qualité optimisées pour la cartographie spatiale, le diagnostic des risques et la modélisation de la sécurité prédictive en aval
• Collaborer via Real-World Pilots: Valider et affiner le pipeline à l'aide de données réelles provenant des villes pilotes du projet, en travaillant en coope proche

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Infrastructure Intervention Effectiveness Analysis for Road Safety

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student. This position focuses on developing intervention effectiveness analysis methodologies to support urban road safety as a part of a larger EU project.

Project background

The new EU Horizon project advances safe active mobility uptake and research by introducing a human-centred, evidence-based approach that integrates actual and perceived safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and micromobility users. Moving beyond conventional crash-focused approaches, it captures near-misses, dynamic interactions, and embodied safety experiences that shape behaviour and mode choice. The project combines multi-source traffic, infrastructure, vehicle, and health data with immersive eXtended Reality (XR) experimentation and explainable Artificial Intelligence to analyse safety-critical situations that are rare, underreported, or ethically impossible to observe in real traffic. Explainable AI ensures transparency and interpretability, supporting trust, transferability, and policy relevance. The project translates these insights into harmonised assessment methodologies, predictive models, and validated indicators, enabling robust evaluation and comparison of regulatory, infrastructural, technological, and behavioural interventions across Safe System Approach stakeholders. Special focus is placed on interactions between users with differing masses and speeds, including e-bikes, e-cargo bikes, and e-scooters, for both personal mobility and urban logistics. Large-scale pilots in four European cities validate methods in real traffic, support cross-city learning, and ensure applicability under diverse safety, infrastructure and cultural conditions. Implemented by a multidisciplinary consortium bridging engineering, behavioural science, XR, AI, urban planning, and policy, the project delivers actionable, standardised guidance that accelerates safer, more inclusive active and micromobility systems across Europe.

Planning safe urban transport systems is inherently complex: interventions last for decades, have widespread impacts, require significant investment, must fit within constrained urban spaces, and must satisfy ever-changing, diverse user needs. Modern data collection and analysis methods are well-suited to capture these complexities by utilizing high-resolution data (e.g., high-frequency measurements from on-board vehicle sensors and computer-vision imagery) to provide near real-time insights. However, it is not yet clear how to effectively operationalize this data to identify high-risk areas, propose targeted infrastructure interventions, and measure their success - largely due to the relative novelty of these data sources, rapid vehicle advancements, and evolving urban mobility patterns.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state-of-the-art in transport infrastructure safety analysis. Working closely with academic, industry, and public authority partners across Europe, the candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Structure Interventions: Structure and model potential infrastructure interventions designed to improve urban safety and comfort

• Develop Indicators: Create robust methodologies and indicators (e.g., surrogate safety measures) to evaluate intervention effectiveness in improving safety and comfort

• Real-World Validation: Apply and test developed frameworks across the project’s four European pilot cities, with a strong focus on the City of Zurich

• Consortium Collaboration: Coordinate regularly with local stakeholders, specifically Zurich’s Dienstabteilung Verkehr (DAV), and international project partners

Profile

• A Master’s degree i

PhD Posizione nell'Infrastruttura Analisi dell'efficacia dell'intervento per la sicurezza stradale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Gestione delle Infrastrutture, guidata dal Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di Costruzione e Gestione delle Infrastrutture del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Ambientale e Geomatica, ha un'apertura per uno studente di dottorato. Questa posizione si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodologie di analisi dell'efficacia degli interventi per sostenere la sicurezza stradale urbana nell'ambito di un progetto UE più ampio. Sfondo del progetto Il nuovo progetto EU Horizon promuove l'assorbimento e la ricerca di una mobilità attiva sicura introducendo un approccio basato su prove umane che integra la sicurezza reale e percepita per pedoni, ciclisti e utenti di micromobilità. Passando oltre i convenzionali approcci focalizzati agli urti, cattura vicino-misses, interazioni dinamiche e esperienze di sicurezza incarnate che modellano il comportamento e la scelta della modalità. Il progetto combina il traffico multi-fonte, l'infrastruttura, il veicolo e i dati sanitari con la sperimentazione immersiva eXtended Reality (XR) e l'intelligenza artificiale spiegabile per analizzare situazioni di sicurezza-critical che sono rare, sottovalutate, o eticamente impossibili da osservare nel traffico reale. La Spiegabile AI garantisce trasparenza e interpretabilità, sostenendo fiducia, trasferibilità e rilevanza politica. Il progetto traduce queste intuizioni in metodologie di valutazione armonizzate, modelli predittivi e indicatori convalidati, consentendo una valutazione e un confronto robusti di interventi normativi, infrastrutturali, tecnologici e comportamentali tra gli stakeholder di Safe System Approach. Particolare attenzione è posta sulle interazioni tra utenti con diverse masse e velocità, tra cui e-bike, e-cargo bike, e-scooters, sia per la mobilità personale che per la logistica urbana. I piloti su larga scala in quattro città europee convalidano i metodi nel traffico reale, supportano l'apprendimento trasversale e garantiscono l'applicabilità in diverse condizioni di sicurezza, infrastruttura e cultura. Implementato da un'ingegneria multidisciplinare di collegamento consortile, scienza comportamentale, XR, AI, pianificazione urbana e politica, il progetto offre una guida attuabile e standardizzata che accelera sistemi attivi e di micromobilità più sicuri e inclusivi in tutta Europa. La pianificazione di sistemi di trasporto urbano sicuri è intrinsecamente complessa: gli interventi durano da decenni, hanno impatti molto diffusi, richiedono un investimento significativo, devono adattarsi all'interno di spazi urbani limitati, e devono soddisfare esigenze di utenti sempre mutevoli e diversificate. I moderni metodi di raccolta e analisi dei dati sono adatti per catturare queste complessità utilizzando dati ad alta risoluzione (ad esempio, misurazioni ad alta frequenza da sensori di veicolo on-board e immagini di computer-visione) per fornire approfondimenti in tempo reale. Tuttavia, non è ancora chiaro come operare efficacemente questi dati per identificare aree ad alto rischio, proporre interventi infrastrutturali mirati e misurare il loro successo - in gran parte a causa della relativa novità di queste fonti di dati, progressi rapidi del veicolo e modelli di mobilità urbana in evoluzione. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a promuovere lo stato dell'arte nell'analisi della sicurezza delle infrastrutture di trasporto. Lavorando a stretto contatto con partner accademici, industriali e di autorità pubbliche in tutta Europa, i compiti principali del candidato includono:
• Interventi Strutturali: Struttura e modelli potenziali interventi infrastrutturali volti a migliorare la sicurezza e il comfort urbano
• Sviluppare indicatori: creare metodologie e indicatori robusti (ad esempio, misure di sicurezza surrogate) per valutare l'efficacia degli interventi nel migliorare la sicurezza e il comfort
• Validazione Real-World: Applicare e testare i quadri sviluppati nelle quattro città pilota europee del progetto, con un forte focus sulla città di Zurigo
• Consorzio Collaborazione: Coordinate regolarmente con gli stakeholder locali, in particolare Dienstabteilung Verkehr (DAV) di Zurigo e partner internazionali di progetto Profilo
• Un master i

Une attention particulière est accordée aux interactions entre les utilisateurs avec des masses et des vitesses différentes, y compris les vélos électroniques, les vélos e-cargo et les e-cooters, pour la mobilité personnelle et la logistique urbaine. Des projets pilotes de grande envergure dans quatre villes européennes valident des méthodes de trafic réel, soutiennent l'apprentissage interurbain et garantissent leur applicabilité dans des conditions de sécurité, d'infrastructure et de culture diverses. Mis en œuvre par un consortium multidisciplinaire d'ingénierie, de science comportementale, de XR, d'IA, d'urbanisme et de politique, le projet fournit des orientations concrètes et standardisées qui accélèrent des systèmes actifs plus sûrs, plus inclusifs et de micromobilité dans toute l'Europe. La planification de systèmes de transport urbain sûrs est intrinsèquement complexe : les interventions durent des décennies, elles ont des effets généralisés, nécessitent des investissements importants, doivent s'intégrer dans des espaces urbains restreints et doivent répondre à des besoins changeants et diversifiés des utilisateurs. Les méthodes modernes de collecte et d'analyse des données sont bien adaptées pour saisir ces complexités en utilisant des données à haute résolution (p. ex. mesures à haute fréquence à partir de capteurs embarqués et d'images de vision par ordinateur) pour fournir des informations en temps quasi réel. Toutefois, il n'est pas encore clair comment rendre ces données efficaces pour identifier les zones à haut risque, proposer des interventions ciblées en matière d'infrastructure et mesurer leur succès - en grande partie en raison de la nouveauté relative de ces sources de données, des progrès rapides des véhicules et de l'évolution des modes de mobilité urbaine. Description de l'emploi Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'analyse de la sécurité des infrastructures de transport. En étroite collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, industriels et publics de toute l'Europe, les tâches essentielles du candidat seront les suivantes:
• Interventions structurelles : Structures et modèles d'interventions potentielles en matière d'infrastructures destinées à améliorer la sécurité et le confort urbains
• Mettre au point des indicateurs: Créer des méthodologies et des indicateurs robustes (par exemple, mesures de sûreté de substitution) pour évaluer l'efficacité de l'intervention dans l'amélioration de la sécurité et du confort
• Validation Real-World: Appliquer et tester des cadres développés dans le cadre du projet dans quatre villes pilotes européennes, avec un accent particulier sur la ville de Zurich
• Collaboration avec les consortiums : Coordonner régulièrement avec les acteurs locaux, en particulier Zurich, Dienstabteilung Verkehr (DAV), et les partenaires internationaux du projet Profil
• Maîtrise i

PhD position in Multi-State Programmable Robotic Matter

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student to work on programmable materials that access multiple distinct mechanical states for next-generation robotic matter systems. This 4-year PhD position is fully funded.

Project background

Modern robots increasingly rely on sophisticated mechanisms, such as modular architectures, reconfigurable linkages, deployable structures, and variable-stiffness components, to adapt their bodies to different tasks and environments. However, such adaptability is often achieved by changing geometry, connectivity, or control strategies, while the underlying material properties remain largely fixed.

This project explores a more fundamental route: robotic matter whose constitutive properties can be programmed on demand. By enabling mechanical modulus, viscoelastic response, and flow behavior to be reconfigured within a single continuous body, we aim to move beyond adaptive hardware architectures towards materials that actively participate in robotic function. The long-term vision is to create robots that can tune their physical embodiment through the programmable properties of matter itself.

Job description

• Design, synthesis, and rheological characterization of dynamic covalent polymer composites targeting programmable mechanical state transitions

• Development of theoretical understanding and multiphysics simulation of material behavior across mechanical regimes

• Fabrication and integration of materials into soft robotic demonstrators showcasing multi-state control under external stimuli

• Development of spatial addressability strategies to achieve localized state modulation in a continuous material body

• Demonstration of robotic functions (locomotion, grasping, navigation through constrictions) that exploit multi-state material behavior

• Supervision of bachelor/master students and participation in teaching

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• MS degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Polymer Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a leading university

• Strong research track record in one or more of the following: dynamic covalent networks, phase-change materials, rheology of complex materials, stimuli-responsive polymers, or soft robotics

• Enthusiasm for fundamental materials challenges with a drive toward robotic applications

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and comfort with interdisciplinary work spanning chemistry, mechanics, and robotics

• Experience with polymer synthesis, mechanical testing, or material fabrication is a strong plus

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

Questa posizione PhD di 4 anni è completamente finanziata. Tuttavia, tale adattabilità è spesso raggiunta cambiando la geometria, la connettività o le strategie di controllo, mentre le proprietà dei materiali sottostanti rimangono in gran parte fissate. Questo progetto esplora un percorso più fondamentale: la materia robotica le cui proprietà costitutive possono essere programmate a richiesta. Con l'attivazione del modulo meccanico, della risposta viscoelastica e del comportamento del flusso da riconfigurare all'interno di un unico corpo continuo, ci proponiamo di andare oltre le architetture hardware adattative verso materiali che partecipano attivamente alla funzione robotica. Descrizione del lavoro - Progettazione, sintesi e caratterizzazione reologica dei compositi polimeri covalenti dinamici che mirano alle transizioni di stato meccanico programmabili - Sviluppo della comprensione teorica e simulazione multifisica del comportamento materiale attraverso i regimi meccanici - La fabbricazione e l'integrazione dei materiali in morbidi dimostranti robotizzati che mostrano il controllo multi-stato sotto stimoli esterni - Sviluppo di strategie di indirizzabilità spaziale per raggiungere modulazione di stato localizzata in un corpo materiale continuo - Laurea in Scienze e Ingegneria dei Materiali, Chimica Polimeri, Ingegneria Meccanica, o campi correlati da un'università leader - Forte tracciato di ricerca in una o più delle seguenti: reti covalenti dinamiche, materiali a cambio di fase, reologia di materiali complessi, polimeri a risposta stimolante, o robotica morbida - Enthusiasm per le sfide materiali fondamentali con una spinta verso applicazioni robotiche - Eccellente capacità di problem solving e comfort con lavoro interdisciplinare che spazia la chimica, la meccanica e la robotica - L'esperienza con sintesi polimerica, collaudo meccanico o fabbricazione di materiale è un forte plus Lavoro - Un ambiente di lavoro produttivo con formazione e guida dal PI regolarmente - stipendio competitivo secondo gli standard ETH (situazione a tempo pieno, a termine fisso) - Un team interdisciplinare, internazionale e diversificato di talenti e un gruppo stimolante, vibrante e collaborativo - forti connessioni con partner accademici, industriali e clinici nella scienza dei materiali, nella robotica e nella sanità Contatto chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo - descriptionByLocale.fr: Poste de doctorat en matière robotique programmable multi-États 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Descrizione Le groupe des matériaux robotiques recherche un doctorant très motivé pour travailler sur des matériaux programmables qui accèdent à de multiples états mécaniques distincts pour les systèmes robotiques de nouvelle génération. Ce poste de doctorat de 4 ans est entièrement financé. Progetto di fond Les robots modernes s'appuient de plus en plus sur des mécanismes sophistiqués, tels que des architectures modulaires, des liens reconfigurables, des structures déployables et des composants à coupe variable, pour adapter leur corps à différentes tâches et environnements. Cependant, une telle adaptabilité est souvent obtenue en modifiant la géométrie, la connectivité ou les stratégies de contrôle, alors que les propriétés matérielles sous-jacentes restent largement fixes. Ce projet explore une voie plus fondamentale : la robotique dont les propriétés constitutives peuvent être programmées sur demande. En permettant la reconfiguration du module mécanique, de la réponse viscoélastique et du comportement d'écoulement au sein d'un seul corps continu, nous visons à dépasser les architectures matérielles adaptatives vers des matériaux qui participent activement à la fonction robotique. La vision à long terme est de créer des robots qui peuvent ajuster leur incarnation physique à travers les propriétés programmables de la matière elle-même. Descrizione del lavoro - Conception, synthèse et caractérisation rhéologique de composites de polymères covalents dynamiques ciblant les transitions mécaniques programmables - Développement de la compréhension théorique et simulation multiphysique du comportement matériel à travers les régimes mécaniques - Fabrication et intégration de matériaux dans des démonstrateurs robotiques souples montrant un contrôle multi-états sous stimuli externes - Élaboration de stratégies d'adressabilité spatiale pour obtenir une modulation d'état localisée dans un corps matériel continu - Démonstration de fonctions robotiques (locomotion, saisie, navigation par constrictions) qui exploitent le comportement matériel multiétat - Supervision des bacheliers/maîtrises et participation à l'enseignement Profil - Maîtrise en sciences des matériaux et génie, chimie des polymères, génie mécanique ou domaines connexes d'une université de premier plan - Forts résultats de recherche dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : réseaux covalents dynamiques, matériaux de changement de phase, rhéologie de matériaux complexes, polymères sensibles aux stimuli ou robotique douce - Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network – Coupled Problems for Decarbonization in Industry and Power Generation (COMBINE)

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network COMBINE brings together 17 academic institutions and 14 industrial partners across Europe.The network addresses key challenges in fluid structure interaction (FSI) relevant to energy, process, and materials engineering, with a strong focus on:

• Advanced numerical modelling and simulation

• Experimental methods and sensor technologies

• Data analysis of real-world monitoring data

• Artificial intelligence and machine learning for engineering applications

Researchers in COMBINE benefit from interdisciplinary, international,and inter-sectoral training, including secondments at leading academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe.

Project background

Project title: High resolution experimental measurements of vibrations in rods and rod bundles using ensemble average high-resolution gamma tomography measurements.

This project focuses on the development of advanced tomographic techniques to evalute vibrations in rod bundles. The research will leverage our in-house, state-of-the-art, high-resolution gamma tomography system.

Job description

• Construction of a setup with a single rod and a rod bundle

• Measurements of vibrating rod/rod-bundle using our in-house gamma-tomography system

• AI-assisted reconstruction and imaging of vibrating rods/bundles using sensors and tomography data

• Use of machine-learning for noise reduction and data enhancement

Profile

• Master's degree in engineering, physics, applied mathematics, computer science, or closely related field

• Strong background in mathematics and machine learning

• Programming proficiency in Python, C++ or similar

• Experience with data processing and model interpretation

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment

• Good written and spoken English

• Hands-on experience with experimental setup and basic electronics understanding is of advantage

Workplace

We offer

• Excellent research environment

• Supervision by internationally recognized academic and industrial experts

• Network-wide training events and local courses in technical and transferable skills

• International secondments at academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe

• Competitive salary

• The research group offices and experimental laboratory are located at Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI), Forschungsstrasse 111, 5232 Villigen

• Metodi sperimentali e tecnologie dei sensori

• Misurazioni dell'asta vibrante/bundle con il nostro sistema gamma-tomografia interno
• Ricostruzione assistita da AI e imaging di barre/bundle vibranti utilizzando sensori e dati di tomografia
• Utilizzo di machine-learning per la riduzione del rumore e il miglioramento dei dati Profilo

Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network – Coupled Problems for Decarbonization in Industry and Power Generation (COMBINE)

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network COMBINE brings together 17 academic institutions and 14 industrial partners across Europe.The network addresses key challenges in fluid structure interaction (FSI) relevant to energy, process, and materials engineering, with a strong focus on:

• Advanced numerical modelling and simulation

• Experimental methods and sensor technologies

• Data analysis of real-world monitoring data

• Artificial intelligence and machine learning for engineering applications

Researchers in COMBINE benefit from interdisciplinary, international,and inter-sectoral training, including secondments at leading academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe.

Project background

Project title: High resolution experimental measurements of vibrations in rods and rod bundles using ensemble average high-resolution gamma tomography measurements.

This project focuses on the development of advanced tomographic techniques to evalute vibrations in rod bundles. The research will leverage our in-house, state-of-the-art, high-resolution gamma tomography system.

Job description

• Construction of a setup with a single rod and a rod bundle

• Measurements of vibrating rod/rod-bundle using our in-house gamma-tomography system

• AI-assisted reconstruction and imaging of vibrating rods/bundles using sensors and tomography data

• Use of machine-learning for noise reduction and data enhancement

Profile

• Master's degree in engineering, physics, applied mathematics, computer science, or closely related field

• Strong background in mathematics and machine learning

• Programming proficiency in Python, C++ or similar

• Experience with data processing and model interpretation

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment

• Good written and spoken English

• Hands-on experience with experimental setup and basic electronics understanding is of advantage

Workplace

We offer

• Excellent research environment

• Supervision by internationally recognized academic and industrial experts

• Network-wide training events and local courses in technical and transferable skills

• International secondments at academic and industrial partner institutions across Europe

• Competitive salary

• The research group offices and experimental laboratory are located at Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI), Forschungsstrasse 111, 5232 Villigen

jobs.description:
MaP Executive Director

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zürich Competence Center for Materials and Processes ( MaP ) is a multidisciplinary scientific network devoted to tackling the grand challenges in materials, processes and manufacturing technologies. We foster cross-disciplinary research, education, and outreach to other academic institutes, industry and society in this field. Current major initiatives of MaP are the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP continuing education programme. To lead the executive office as the central coordination hub, MaP is currently hiring a new Executive Director, starting from 1 July 2026 or earlier on agreement.

Project background

We are seeking an individual who is highly motivated to manage and develop MaP , together with the Steering Committee and the community of over 80 affiliated research groups . The Executive Director is responsible for leading the executive office, including managing strategy, human resources, finances, as well as operations and activities, governance and communications. The main focus of this key interfacing role is on community building and managing multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes, therefore requiring a broad understanding of the grand challenges in Materials and Processes. The position embraces the designing, managing and overseeing of all research, education and outreach programs of MaP , including the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP .

Job description

Strategic Leadership & Office Management

• Manage and develop MaP in close collaboration with the Steering Committee and a community of over 80 affiliated research groups.

• Lead the executive office, taking full responsibility for its operations and daily activities.

• Oversee core management areas, including strategy, human resources, finances, and governance.

Collaboration & Community Building

• Foster community building and manage multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes.

• Act as a key interface between various research groups and research entities.

• Direct/Develop communication strategies to engage and connect the MaP community.

Program Management & Oversight

• Design, manage, and oversee all MaP research, education, and outreach programs.

• Direct specific initiatives, including the MaP Doctoral School and the ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP.

Profile

• The successful candidate has a strong academic background in science and/or engineering and ample work experience in topics relevant to Materials and Processes.

• Given the requirement to work across disciplines, sectors and cultures, the candidate must have excellent communication and organisational skills and experience in community building and further participatory processes.

• Strong project and business management skills are essential, from strategy and conceptualisation to planning and effective implementation, along with budgeting, financial management, evaluation and reporting.

• The ability to work in a motivated, independent, responsible, resourceful and resilient manner is vital.

• And, ideally, the candidate has already gained some hands-on experience in managing people, having budget responsibility and running research projects and education programs. Fluency in English and German is required.

Workplace

We offer

We offer a dynamic work environment with a high degree of freedom in design and implementation and many opportunities for an individual with commensurate qualifications, a can-do attitude, and a proactive and creative mindset to further her/his professional goals. The position is limited to one year, with the possibility of extension depending on the further development of MaP and its initiatives.

• Il candidato avverso ha un solido background accademico in scienza e/o ingegneria e una vasta esperienza professionale in materia di Materiali e Processi.

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Light-Driven CO2 Capture

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Electrochemical Energy Systems Laboratory in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position focused on light-driven CO2 capture.

Job description

• Our group is actively developing a novel photoacid-based approach for efficient CO2 capture, optimizing both the local chemical environment in photoacids and their molecular structure to enhance sorption capacity and stability

• We seek a postdoctoral researcher who will contribute to these efforts

• You will join a diverse, inclusive, and supportive work environment that values scientific curiosity and creativity

Profile

• PhD in Physical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or a related field

• Experience with in situ spectroscopy is a plus

• Excellent written and spoken English

• Self-driven, highly motivated, and strong teamwork skills

We welcome applications from candidates with expertise in organic synthesis and one or more of the following areas:

• Photochemistry

• Advanced characterization techniques (e.g., synchrotron facilities, in-situ methods)

• CO2 capture / utilization is a plus

We are looking for highly motivated researchers with a passion for contributing to solutions in the global energy landscape. If you excel in collaborative environments and can bring expertise in some of the areas listed above, we encourage you to apply.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application please submit the following documents as a single merged PDF named with your last name, initials, and application date (e.g., 20250206_SmithJT_application) in the following order:

• Cover Letter describing your research achievements and interests

• Detailed CV

• Three Representative Published Works

• Names and Contact Information of at Least Three References

• Official Transcripts of All Degrees or a PhD degree confirmation, if available (in English)

In the field for additional information, please include your PhD, MSc, and BSc degree details (university, dates, and relevant experience).

Further information about our group can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Melanie Darugna, mdarugna@ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

This is a full-time position, tentatively starting on 15 July 2026, or later. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

Research Division KOF Lab of ETH Zurich’s KOF Swiss Economic Institute is seeking a PhD candidate to study the propagation of weather and climate shocks in quantitative trade network models. The position is part of the National Centre of Competence in Research project Climate Extremes and Society: Strengthening Resilience (NCCR CLIM+). NCCR CLIM+ is a new, interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community involving multiple investigators at ETH Zurich and other Swiss institutions.

Job description

• The project at KOF Lab will center around assessing and promoting the resilience of supply chains by building and solving quantitative global equilibrium models of trade networks.

• We will use firm-level data to estimate the industry/country-level effects of various weather and climate shocks and input the estimated impacts into the model.

• To this end, the doctoral candidate will leverage theoretical, computational, and econometric tools to study public policy questions related to the resilience of global supply chains to climate change.

• The doctorate will be conducted within the doctoral program of D-MTEC (Department of Management, Technology, and Economics) and is expected to be completed within four years.

• The candidate will be supervised primarily by Professor Hans Gersbach and Dr. Kieran Walsh.

• The position is for up to four years. The salary is in accordance with the PhD regulations of the Swiss National Science Foundation, which funds the NCCR.

Profile

• The applicant should have a master’s degree in economics or finance. We will also consider candidates with a master’s degree in mathematics or statistics, provided they have completed some coursework in economics and are prepared to do intensive economics PhD training.

• Applicants must be highly proficient in English.

• The applicant should be proficient in either MATLAB, Python, or Julia and willing to work in MATLAB.

• Prior coursework in (i) trade theory and (ii) environmental economics would be a major asset.

• Experience with panel data econometrics would be beneficial.

Workplace

We offer

• We offer the opportunity to apply cutting-edge economic theory to practical policy issues at the intersection of trade and climate change.

• Candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to NCCR CLIM+ research discussions.

• We offer the opportunity to join KOF, which is Switzerland’s leading academic institute for applied economic research. It provides independent and objective data and facts, as well as timely assessments to support decision-makers in politics and business in making fact-based decisions for the benefit of Swiss society.

• KOF PhD students are part of a large and vibrant community of economic researchers. The broader economics community in Zurich offers the opportunity to participate in numerous workshops and conferences spanning all fields of economics.

jobs.description:
PhD Position in AI-Supported Resilience Assessment of Climate-Neutral Transport Infrastructure

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student in transport infrastructure resilience. The position is part of the EU Horizon project SHIFTIN, which aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050.

The doctoral research will focus on developing AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate-modelling methodologies to assess the resilience of interdependent transport infrastructure systems under climate-related and multi-hazard scenarios. The work will support rapid, evidence-based evaluation of design, retrofit, maintenance, and recovery strategies at asset, corridor, and network scales.

Project background

SHIFTIN is an EU Horizon project that aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050. Roads, railways, and ports are essential for European mobility and economic activity, but they also consume large volumes of raw materials, generate greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, fragment habitats, and are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards such as floods, landslides, and heatwaves.

To address these challenges, SHIFTIN will demonstrate and combine circular low-carbon construction materials, nature-based solutions, advanced monitoring technologies, and digital decision-support tools. Full-scale pilots on four TEN-T corridors will cover road, rail, and port contexts, integrating infrastructure monitoring, satellite and on-board sensing, IoT-enabled structural health monitoring, and AI-supported analytics.

A Digital Twin-based Integrated Decision Support Platform will convert monitoring and modelling outputs into transparent whole-life indicators for carbon, circularity, resilience, biodiversity, and costs. These outputs will support robust business cases, maintenance planning, green public procurement, and the wider uptake of sustainable and resilient infrastructure solutions across European transport networks.

Within this broader project, the PhD research will focus on AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate modelling for transport infrastructure resilience. The goal is to enable rapid assessment of many hazard, disruption, recovery, and intervention scenarios, supporting practical decision-making for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state of the art in simulation-informed, AI-supported resilience assessment for transport infrastructure. Working closely with academic, industry, infrastructure, and public-sector partners across Europe, the candidate will contribute to the development of stress-testing frameworks, surrogate modelling algorithms, and decision-support tools for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Developing AI-supported surrogate models for infrastructure stress testing

• Linking surrogate models with agent-based and network-based simulations

• Assessing infrastructure interdependencies and recovery constraints

• Supporting resilience assessment across asset, corridor, and network scales

• Contributing to cost-benefit and decision-support analysis

• Addressing uncertainty, reliability, and explainability

• Integrating results with digital-twin and monitoring data

• Collaborating with the European project consortium

Profile

• A Master’s degree in civil engineering, transport engineering, infrastructure systems, environmental engineering, computational engineering, data science, or a closely related field

• Strong quantitative and programming skills, preferably

Posizione di dottorato in valutazione della resilienza supportata dall'intelligenza artificiale di infrastrutture di trasporto a impatto climatico zero 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Drucken La cattedra di gestione delle infrastrutture, guidata dal professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di costruzione e gestione delle infrastrutture del Dipartimento di ingegneria civile, ambientale e geomatica, ha un posto vacante per uno studente di dottorato in resilienza delle infrastrutture di trasporto. La posizione fa parte del progetto EU Horizon SHIFTIN, che mira ad accelerare la transizione verso infrastrutture di trasporto climaticamente neutre, resilienti e rispettose della biodiversità entro il 2050. La ricerca di dottorato si concentrerà sullo sviluppo di stress test supportati dall'intelligenza artificiale e di metodologie di modellazione surrogata per valutare la resilienza dei sistemi infrastrutturali di trasporto interdipendenti in scenari legati al clima e multi-rischio. Il lavoro supporterà una valutazione rapida e basata sull’evidenza delle strategie di progettazione, ammodernamento, manutenzione e ripristino a livello di asset, corridoio e rete. Contesto del progetto SHIFTIN è un progetto Horizon dell’UE che mira ad accelerare la transizione verso infrastrutture di trasporto climaticamente neutre, resilienti e rispettose della biodiversità entro il 2050. Strade, ferrovie e porti sono essenziali per la mobilità e l’attività economica europea, ma consumano anche grandi volumi di materie prime, generano emissioni di gas serra e inquinanti atmosferici, frammentano gli habitat e sono sempre più esposti a rischi legati al clima come inondazioni, frane e ondate di caldo. Per affrontare queste sfide, SHIFTIN dimostrerà e combinerà materiali da costruzione circolari a basse emissioni di carbonio, soluzioni basate sulla natura, tecnologie di monitoraggio avanzate e strumenti digitali di supporto alle decisioni. I progetti pilota su vasta scala su quattro corridoi TEN-T copriranno contesti stradali, ferroviari e portuali, integrando il monitoraggio delle infrastrutture, il rilevamento satellitare e di bordo, il monitoraggio della salute strutturale abilitato dall’IoT e l’analisi supportata dall’intelligenza artificiale. Una piattaforma integrata di supporto alle decisioni basata sul digital twin convertirà i risultati del monitoraggio e della modellazione in indicatori trasparenti per l’intero ciclo vitale di carbonio, circolarità, resilienza, biodiversità e costi. Questi risultati supporteranno solidi casi aziendali, pianificazione della manutenzione, appalti pubblici verdi e una più ampia adozione di soluzioni infrastrutturali sostenibili e resilienti nelle reti di trasporto europee. All’interno di questo progetto più ampio, la ricerca di dottorato si concentrerà sugli stress test supportati dall’intelligenza artificiale e sulla modellizzazione surrogata per la resilienza delle infrastrutture di trasporto. L’obiettivo è consentire una rapida valutazione di molti scenari di pericolo, interruzione, ripresa e intervento, supportando il processo decisionale pratico per sistemi di trasporto resilienti al clima e sostenibili. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a far avanzare lo stato dell'arte nella valutazione della resilienza basata sulla simulazione e supportata dall'intelligenza artificiale per le infrastrutture di trasporto. Lavorando a stretto contatto con partner accademici, industriali, infrastrutturali e del settore pubblico in tutta Europa, il candidato contribuirà allo sviluppo di quadri di stress test, algoritmi di modellazione surrogati e strumenti di supporto decisionale per sistemi di trasporto resilienti al clima e sostenibili. I compiti principali del candidato includeranno:
• Sviluppare modelli surrogati supportati dall'intelligenza artificiale per stress test delle infrastrutture
• Collegare modelli surrogati con simulazioni basate su agenti e su rete
• Valutare le interdipendenze delle infrastrutture e i vincoli di ripristino
• Supportare la valutazione della resilienza su scale di risorse, corridoi e reti
• Contribuire all'analisi costi-benefici e di supporto alle decisioni
• Affrontare l'incertezza, l'affidabilità e la spiegabilità

PhD Position in AI-Supported Resilience Assessment of Climate-Neutral Transport Infrastructure

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student in transport infrastructure resilience. The position is part of the EU Horizon project SHIFTIN, which aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050.

The doctoral research will focus on developing AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate-modelling methodologies to assess the resilience of interdependent transport infrastructure systems under climate-related and multi-hazard scenarios. The work will support rapid, evidence-based evaluation of design, retrofit, maintenance, and recovery strategies at asset, corridor, and network scales.

Project background

SHIFTIN is an EU Horizon project that aims to accelerate the transition towards climate-neutral, resilient, and biodiversity-friendly transport infrastructure by 2050. Roads, railways, and ports are essential for European mobility and economic activity, but they also consume large volumes of raw materials, generate greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, fragment habitats, and are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards such as floods, landslides, and heatwaves.

To address these challenges, SHIFTIN will demonstrate and combine circular low-carbon construction materials, nature-based solutions, advanced monitoring technologies, and digital decision-support tools. Full-scale pilots on four TEN-T corridors will cover road, rail, and port contexts, integrating infrastructure monitoring, satellite and on-board sensing, IoT-enabled structural health monitoring, and AI-supported analytics.

A Digital Twin-based Integrated Decision Support Platform will convert monitoring and modelling outputs into transparent whole-life indicators for carbon, circularity, resilience, biodiversity, and costs. These outputs will support robust business cases, maintenance planning, green public procurement, and the wider uptake of sustainable and resilient infrastructure solutions across European transport networks.

Within this broader project, the PhD research will focus on AI-supported stress-testing and surrogate modelling for transport infrastructure resilience. The goal is to enable rapid assessment of many hazard, disruption, recovery, and intervention scenarios, supporting practical decision-making for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state of the art in simulation-informed, AI-supported resilience assessment for transport infrastructure. Working closely with academic, industry, infrastructure, and public-sector partners across Europe, the candidate will contribute to the development of stress-testing frameworks, surrogate modelling algorithms, and decision-support tools for climate-resilient and sustainable transport systems. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Developing AI-supported surrogate models for infrastructure stress testing

• Linking surrogate models with agent-based and network-based simulations

• Assessing infrastructure interdependencies and recovery constraints

• Supporting resilience assessment across asset, corridor, and network scales

• Contributing to cost-benefit and decision-support analysis

• Addressing uncertainty, reliability, and explainability

• Integrating results with digital-twin and monitoring data

• Collaborating with the European project consortium

Profile

• A Master’s degree in civil engineering, transport engineering, infrastructure systems, environmental engineering, computational engineering, data science, or a closely related field

• Strong quantitative and programming skills, preferably

Poste de doctorat en évaluation de la résilience des infrastructures de transport climatiquement neutres par l'IA à 100 %, Zurich, impression à durée déterminée Drucken La chaire de gestion des infrastructures, dirigée par le professeur Dr Bryan T. Adey au sein de l'Institut de construction et de gestion des infrastructures du Département de génie civil, environnemental et géomatique, a une ouverture pour un doctorant en résilience des infrastructures de transport. Le poste fait partie du projet Horizon de l'UE SHIFTIN, qui vise à accélérer la transition vers des infrastructures de transport neutres pour le climat, résilientes et respectueuses de la biodiversité d'ici 2050. La recherche doctorale se concentrera sur le développement de méthodologies de tests de résistance et de modélisation de substitution basées sur l'IA pour évaluer la résilience des systèmes d'infrastructures de transport interdépendants dans des scénarios liés au climat et à plusieurs risques. Les travaux soutiendront une évaluation rapide et fondée sur des données probantes des stratégies de conception, de modernisation, de maintenance et de récupération à l’échelle des actifs, des corridors et du réseau. Contexte du projet SHIFTIN est un projet Horizon de l'UE qui vise à accélérer la transition vers des infrastructures de transport neutres pour le climat, résilientes et respectueuses de la biodiversité d'ici 2050. Les routes, les chemins de fer et les ports sont essentiels à la mobilité et à l'activité économique européennes, mais ils consomment également de grandes quantités de matières premières, génèrent des émissions de gaz à effet de serre et de polluants atmosphériques, fragmentent les habitats et sont de plus en plus exposés aux risques liés au climat tels que les inondations, les glissements de terrain et les vagues de chaleur. Pour relever ces défis, SHIFTIN démontrera et combinera des matériaux de construction circulaires à faible émission de carbone, des solutions basées sur la nature, des technologies de surveillance avancées et des outils numériques d'aide à la décision. Des projets pilotes à grande échelle sur quatre corridors RTE-T couvriront les contextes routiers, ferroviaires et portuaires, intégrant la surveillance des infrastructures, la détection par satellite et embarquée, la surveillance de l'état des structures grâce à l'IoT et les analyses basées sur l'IA. Une plateforme intégrée d'aide à la décision basée sur un jumeau numérique convertira les résultats de la surveillance et de la modélisation en indicateurs transparents sur toute la durée de vie du carbone, de la circularité, de la résilience, de la biodiversité et des coûts. Ces résultats soutiendront des analyses de rentabilisation solides, la planification de la maintenance, les marchés publics écologiques et l'adoption plus large de solutions d'infrastructure durables et résilientes dans les réseaux de transport européens. Dans le cadre de ce projet plus large, la recherche doctorale se concentrera sur les tests de résistance et la modélisation de substitution basés sur l'IA pour la résilience des infrastructures de transport. L’objectif est de permettre une évaluation rapide de nombreux scénarios de danger, de perturbation, de rétablissement et d’intervention, aidant ainsi la prise de décision pratique pour des systèmes de transport durables et résilients au climat. Description du poste Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de l'art en matière d'évaluation de la résilience des infrastructures de transport, basée sur la simulation et appuyée par l'IA. Travaillant en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, industriels, infrastructurels et du secteur public à travers l'Europe, le candidat contribuera au développement de cadres de tests de résistance, d'algorithmes de modélisation de substitution et d'outils d'aide à la décision pour des systèmes de transport durables et résilients au climat. jobs.description:
PhD position in Computational earthquake rupture mechanics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure.

Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics.

We are seeking a motivated, innovative PhD student with a background in computational mechanics to work on a project in computational earthquake rupture mechanics. The project will combine numerical method development and theoretical analysis to investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear near-fault processes influence earthquake rupture propagation, arrest, and earthquake-size statistics.

Job description

• You will conduct a computational and theoretical investigation of dynamic earthquake rupture, with a focus on rupture propagation, rupture arrest, and energy dissipation in heterogeneous fault systems

• The work will connect fracture-mechanics theory with large-scale numerical simulations of earthquake rupture

• You will develop, improve, and use high-performance simulation tools for dynamic rupture, including GPU-oriented numerical methods

• You will verify and validate the numerical methods against benchmark problems and established theoretical results

• Building on these tools, you will investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear dissipative processes, such as off-fault plasticity, influence rupture arrest and earthquake-size statistics

• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration

Profile

• You hold an MSc degree in mechanics, physics, engineering, earth science, material science, computational science, or a related discipline

• You have a background in computational mechanics, solid mechanics, applied physics, scientific computing, or a related field

• You have experience implementing scientific code and validating it against analytical solutions, numerical benchmarks, or well-documented reference results.

• You have prior programming experience in Python and have used version control. Experience with high-performance computing, GPU programming, C/C++, or numerical methods for wave propagation, fracture, or solid mechanics is an advantage

• You are curious, self-motivated, and enjoy developing numerical methods to answer mechanics questions

• You are fluent in English, both oral and written

• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere

Workplace

We offer

• You will join a dynamic, international, and supportive research group that values curiosity, rigor, and collaboration.

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively

descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Alla cattedra di Meccanica dei Solidi (SMEC) presso l'Istituto dei Materiali da Costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, miriamo a capire come i materiali si deformano, si degradano, si rompono e, infine, si guastano. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità verso i meccanismi fisici che sono alla base dei cedimenti e dall’ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando modellazione numerica, esperimenti di laboratorio e analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico sia dei sistemi ingegneristici che naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per i guasti meccanici. Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale e riunisce ricercatori con background in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo su un'ampia gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidali e granulari), materiali strutturati e topologicamente interconnessi, la meccanica della fragilità del collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura di materiali morbidi e la modellazione dei guasti in processi multifisici come il degrado del calcestruzzo causato dalla corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l’impegno nello sviluppo di nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che migliorino la nostra comprensione dei meccanismi dei guasti.
• Cerchiamo uno studente di dottorato motivato e innovativo con un background in meccanica computazionale per lavorare su un progetto sulla meccanica computazionale della rottura dei terremoti. Il progetto combinerà lo sviluppo di metodi numerici e l’analisi teorica per studiare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e i processi non lineari di quasi faglia influenzano la propagazione della rottura del terremoto, l’arresto e le statistiche sulle dimensioni del terremoto. Descrizione del lavoro - Condurre un'indagine computazionale e teorica sulla rottura dinamica del terremoto, con particolare attenzione alla propagazione della rottura, all'arresto della rottura e alla dissipazione di energia in sistemi di faglie eterogenei - Collegare la teoria della meccanica della frattura con simulazioni numeriche su larga scala della rottura del terremoto - Sviluppare, migliorare e utilizzare strumenti di simulazione ad alte prestazioni per la rottura dinamica, inclusi metodi numerici orientati alla GPU - Verificare e convalidare i metodi numerici rispetto a problemi di riferimento e risultati teorici consolidati - Investigare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e processi dissipativi non lineari, come plasticità fuori faglia, arresto di rottura e statistiche sulle dimensioni dei terremoti - Fornire un ambiente stimolante per la crescita scientifica e la collaborazione Profilo - Possedere un master in meccanica, fisica, ingegneria, scienze della terra, scienza dei materiali, scienze computazionali o una disciplina correlata - Avere esperienza in meccanica computazionale, meccanica dei solidi, fisica applicata, informatica scientifica o un campo correlato - Avere esperienza nell'implementazione di codice scientifico e nella sua convalida rispetto a soluzioni analitiche, benchmark numerici o risultati di riferimento ben documentati - Avere esperienza di programmazione precedente in Python e hanno utilizzato il controllo della versione. L'esperienza con il calcolo ad alte prestazioni, la programmazione GPU, C/C++ o metodi numerici per la propagazione delle onde, la frattura o la meccanica dei solidi costituisce un vantaggio - Essere curioso, automotivato e divertirsi nello sviluppo di metodi numerici per rispondere a domande di meccanica - Essere fluente in inglese, sia orale che scritto - Piacere lavorare in gruppo, possedere le necessarie abilità sociali e comunicative e contribuire in modo proattivo a un'atmosfera di gruppo positiva Cosa offerta - Partecipa a un gruppo di ricerca dinamico, internazionale e solidale che valorizza la curiosità, il rigore e la collaborazione - Il tuo lavoro ha un impatto: diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo sostiene il tuo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce anche attivamente alla tua crescita professionale e al tuo successo

descriptionByLocale.de: Beschreibung: An der Professur für Festkörpermechanik (SMEC) am Institut für Baustoffe der ETH Zürich wollen wir verstehen, wie sich Materialien verformen, zersetzen, brechen und letztendlich versagen. Unsere Forschung basiert auf der Neugier auf die physikalischen Mechanismen, die einem Versagen zugrunde liegen, und dem Ehrgeiz, dieses Verständnis in zuverlässigere und widerstandsfähigere Materialien und Strukturen umzusetzen. Durch die Kombination numerischer Modellierung, Laborexperimente und theoretischer Analysen versuchen wir, mikroskopische Prozesse mit dem makroskopischen Verhalten sowohl technischer als auch natürlicher Systeme zu verknüpfen und Vorhersagewerkzeuge für mechanisches Versagen zu entwickeln. Unser Team ist äußerst interdisziplinär und international und vereint Forscher mit Hintergrund in den Materialwissenschaften, der Mechanik und der angewandten Physik. Wir arbeiten zu einem breiten Themenspektrum, darunter die Mechanik von Partikelsystemen (kolloidal und körnig), architektonische und topologisch ineinandergreifende Materialien, die Mechanik der Zerbrechlichkeit von Kollagen, die Mechanik von Erdbeben, den Bruch weicher Materialien und die Modellierung von Fehlern in multiphysikalischen Prozessen wie der korrosionsbedingten Zersetzung von Beton. Was diese Bemühungen vereint, ist die gemeinsame Neugier, warum komplexe Materialien versagen, und das Engagement für die Entwicklung neuer Konzepte, Experimente und Modelle, die unser Verständnis der Versagensmechanik verbessern. Wir suchen einen motivierten, innovativen Doktoranden mit einem Hintergrund in computergestützter Mechanik, der an einem Projekt zur rechnergestützten Erdbeben-Bruchmechanik arbeitet. Das Projekt wird die Entwicklung numerischer Methoden und theoretische Analysen kombinieren, um zu untersuchen, wie heterogene Spannungszustände und nichtlineare fehlernahe Prozesse die Ausbreitung, den Stillstand und die Erdbebengrößenstatistik von Erdbebenbrüchen beeinflussen. Stellenbeschreibung - Führen Sie eine rechnerische und theoretische Untersuchung des dynamischen Erdbebenbruchs durch, mit Schwerpunkt auf Bruchausbreitung, Bruchstopp und Energiedissipation in heterogenen Verwerfungssystemen. - Verbinden Sie die Theorie der Bruchmechanik mit groß angelegten numerischen Simulationen des Erdbebenbruchs nichtlineare dissipative Prozesse wie Off-Fault-Plastizität, Influencer-Rupture-Arrest und Erdbebengrößenstatistiken - Bieten Sie ein stimulierendes Umfeld für wissenschaftliches Wachstum und Zusammenarbeit.
