Laboratory engineer: in power electronics and drive systems (m/f/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, temporary Printed Printing The Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (D‐ITET) at ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading research and training institutes in the fields of electrical engineering and information technology. His research activities range from integrated circuits and computer networks to wireless communication, signal processing and control technology to electrical energy technology. The department offers a highly interdisciplinary research environment with proven expertise in power electronic components and power converters, electric drives, electrical insulation technology and the modeling of complex technical systems. Project background The Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS) Laboratory at ETH Zurich is researching innovative solutions for power electronics, electric drives and future energy systems. Research activities range from novel transducer and drive concepts for electromobility to highly dynamic power electronics for future data centers to cryogenic converter systems for feeding superconducting magnets. Advanced Mechatronic Systems Group (AMS) researches integrated mechatronic systems, including electromagnetic actuators, sensors, electrical machines, control technology, system integration and related fields. To strengthen our team, we are looking for a dedicated laboratory engineer with a strong hands-on mentality and enjoyment of challenging technical challenges. Job description As a laboratory engineer, you will play a central role in setting up and further developing the research laboratory of the Power Electronics and Drive Systems Laboratory and the Advanced Mechatronic Systems Group. They support researchers in the implementation of challenging experimental projects and contribute to the long-term technical development of the groups. In particular, its tasks include:
• Establishment, further development and operation of laboratory infrastructure for research and teaching
• Support for doctoral candidates, postdocs and students in realizing experimental research projects
• Planning, realisation, commissioning and optimisation of prototypes and test stands
• Support in the areas of power electronics, metrology, PCB design and embedded systems
• Responsibility for laboratory organisation, equipment management and technical documentation
• Function as group security representative: in and participation in the establishment of safe and efficient laboratory processes
• Securing and transferring technical know-how within the research group The position offers the opportunity to actively shape the development of a young and growing research group and to shape its technical development in the long term. Profile Degree & Experience:
• You have completed your studies (FH/ETH/TU) in electrical engineering or a related field
• Practical experience in power electronics, electronics development, embedded systems or related technical disciplines Ideally, you will bring experience in several of the following areas:
• Power electronics, electric drive systems and mechatronic systems
• Laboratory and measurement technology with focus on power electronics
• Construction and commissioning of prototypes
• PCB design (e.g. Altium, KiCAD or equivalent)
• Embedded systems and microcontroller programming (e.g. STM32 and AMD Zynq)
• Debugging of analogue and digital circuits Softskills & Languages:
• You work independently, structured and solution-oriented,

Ingénieur de laboratoire: en électronique de puissance et systèmes d'entraînement (m/f/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, temporaire Imprimé Impression Le Département des technologies de l'information et du génie électrique (D‐ITET) de l'ETH Zurich est l'un des principaux instituts de recherche et de formation dans les domaines du génie électrique et des technologies de l'information. Ses activités de recherche vont des circuits intégrés et des réseaux informatiques aux technologies de communication sans fil, de traitement et de contrôle des signaux aux technologies de l'énergie électrique. Le département offre un environnement de recherche hautement interdisciplinaire avec une expertise éprouvée en composants électroniques et convertisseurs de puissance, entraînements électriques, technologie d'isolation électrique et la modélisation de systèmes techniques complexes. Contexte du projet Le laboratoire Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS) de l'ETH Zurich recherche des solutions innovantes pour l'électronique électrique, les entraînements électriques et les futurs systèmes énergétiques. Les activités de recherche vont de nouveaux concepts de transducteur et d'entraînement pour l'électromobilité à l'électronique de puissance très dynamique pour les futurs centres de données à des systèmes de convertisseur cryogénique pour l'alimentation des aimants supraconducteurs. Advanced Mecatronic Systems Group (AMS) étudie les systèmes mécatroniques intégrés, y compris les actionneurs électromagnétiques, les capteurs, les machines électriques, la technologie de contrôle, l'intégration des systèmes et les domaines connexes. Pour renforcer notre équipe, nous sommes à la recherche d'un ingénieur de laboratoire dévoué avec une forte mentalité pratique et la jouissance de défis techniques difficiles. jobs.description:
Data Manager

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

NEXUS Personalized Health is the technology platform for personalized health at ETH Zurich . Since 2015, NEXUS has enabled and accelerated biomedical research by providing scientific expertise and tailored services in clinical bioinformatics, software engineering, biostatistics, high-throughput screening, and data management. Working at the interface between research and clinical application, NEXUS collaborates with researchers from ETH Zurich, hospitals, academia, and industry to develop innovative solutions that advance personalized medicine.

Project background

NEXUS supports two cutting-edge biomedical research projects that rely on robust and secure research data management. Data and metadata are collected from multiple laboratories, stored on the highly secure LeoMed platform, and consolidated within a LabKey installation to provide researchers with high-quality, well-organized datasets.

To cover a maternity leave, we are looking for a Data Manager for a fixed-term appointment of six months. In this role, you will support the day-to-day data management activities of ongoing research projects, ensuring data quality, consistency, and compliance while working closely with researchers.

This is a fixed-term position for 6 months, from September 2026 to February 2027.

Job description

As a Data Manager, you will support biomedical research projects by implementing and maintaining good data management practices. Your responsibilities include:

• Collect, curate and organize research data and metadata from multiple laboratories.

• Ensure data completeness, consistency and quality throughout the project lifecycle.

• Maintain and update metadata within LabKey and related systems.

• Write and maintain scripts (e.g. in Python or Bash) to parse, transform and validate research data.

• Support data synchronization and secure storage on LeoMed.

• Assist researchers with data management questions and documentation.

• Help implement data governance and FAIR data principles within research projects.

• Document data workflows, standards and project procedures.

• Collaborate with software engineers and researchers to improve data management processes.

Profile

Required qualifications

• MSc Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science, Data Science, Life Sciences or a related field.

• Experience working with biomedical or scientific research data.

• Good scripting skills (preferably Python; Bash or similar languages are also welcome) for parsing, transforming and validating data.

• Basic understanding of relational databases and SQL.

• Familiarity with research data management concepts and metadata.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Very good written and spoken English.

Nice to have

• Experience with LeoMed or other secure computing environments.

• Experience using LabKey or similar laboratory information/data management systems.

• Knowledge of FAIR data principles.

• Experience working in collaborative biomedical research projects.

Workplace

We offer

• An opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge biomedical research at ETH Zurich.

• Flexible working hours and the possibility to work partially from home.

• A collegial, interdisciplinary and supportive team.

• A structured onboarding and handover for this temporary position.

• Modern office facilities at the Bio-Technopark Schlieren.

• The opportunity to gain experience with state-of-the-art biomedical data infrastructures and collaborate with leading researchers.

• Attractive employment conditions according to ETH Zurich regulations.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students

Lavorando all'interfaccia tra ricerca e applicazione clinica, NEXUS collabora con i ricercatori di ETH Zurich, ospedali, accademia e industria per sviluppare soluzioni innovative che avanzano la medicina personalizzata. • Esperienza di lavoro con dati di ricerca biomedica o scientifica.
• Buone capacità di scrittura (preferibilmente Python; Bash o lingue simili sono anche benvenuti) per la parsing, la trasformazione e la convalida dei dati.

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher - Forest Management and Economics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

You are excited about forests, data, teaching, and the big question of how we can manage forested landscapes under uncertainty? You enjoy developing your own research ideas, working with students, building collaborations, and turning scientific insights into something useful for research, practice, and society? Then this position might be for you. The Chair of Forest Resources Management FORM at ETH Zurich is looking for a Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. The position combines research, teaching, student supervision, project development, and engagement with a lively scientific and professional network. It is a great opportunity for someone who wants to grow as an independent researcher while contributing to applied, forward-looking forestry research. The FORM group is a dynamic, interdisciplinary research team at ETH Zurich. We work on the question of how forests can be understood, monitored, modelled, and managed today and in the future. Our research connects forest ecology, forest management, remote sensing, decision support, risk analysis, economics, and stakeholder-oriented approaches. We are strongly involved in teaching within the Department of Environmental Systems Science D-USYS. Our courses, practicals, field activities, and student projects cover forest resources management, forest and landscape planning, forest economics, applied decision-making, and the sustainable management of landscapes under changing environmental conditions. We like research that is rigorous, useful, creative, and connected to the real world. We work with data, models, maps, people, forests, students, and partners from science, practice, and administration. Some days are about manuscripts and code; others are about teaching, field discussions, proposal writing, or helping a student find the best way forward.

Job description

• In research, you will develop your own ideas within the wider field of forest management and economics, building on or linking to remote sensing, decision support, and related areas

• You will acquire, clean, analyse, and interpret data, prepare scientific manuscripts, contribute to non-scientific outputs, and present your work at national and international conferences

• You will also play an active role in developing new research proposals

• This includes combining your own scientific interests with the broader research focus of the FORM group, identifying funding opportunities, contributing to proposals as a PI, collaborator, or partner, and helping turn good ideas into funded projects

• In teaching, you will contribute to existing and new courses in the Bachelor’s and Master’s programs in Forest and Landscape Management, particularly Forest Economics

• You will help students understand how ecological, economic, spatial, and societal questions come together when decisions about forests and landscapes are made

• You will supervise student projects

• This includes helping students shape research questions, develop methods, collect and clean data, apply statistical approaches, improve their writing, and move from “I have an idea” to “I have a solid thesis”

• Beyond research and teaching, you will support and sometimes lead the organisation of workshops, meetings, events, and other activities hosted by FORM and D-USYS

• You will help maintain and develop scientific networks and professional alliances, and you will be encouraged to further develop your own skills in project management, supervision, communication, leadership, and collaboration

Profile

• You hold a PhD in forestry, forest sciences, forest economics, environmental sciences with a major in forest and landscape management, or a related field, providing you with solid knowledge about forests

• You have a strong interest in forest management and economics and enjoy working at the interface of science, teachin

Ricercatore post-dottorato - Gestione forestale ed economia 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Siete entusiasti di foreste, dati, insegnamento e la grande domanda di come possiamo gestire i paesaggi boschivi sotto incertezza? Ti piace sviluppare le tue idee di ricerca, lavorare con gli studenti, costruire collaborazioni, e trasformare le intuizioni scientifiche in qualcosa di utile per la ricerca, la pratica e la società? Allora questa posizione potrebbe essere per voi. Il Presidente della Forest Resources Management FORM di ETH Zurich sta cercando un Ricercatore Postdoctoral per unirsi al nostro team. La posizione combina ricerca, insegnamento, supervisione degli studenti, sviluppo del progetto e impegno con una vivace rete scientifica e professionale. È una grande opportunità per qualcuno che vuole crescere come ricercatore indipendente, contribuendo alla ricerca forestale applicata e previsionale. Il gruppo FORM è un team di ricerca dinamico e interdisciplinare dell'ETH di Zurigo. Lavoriamo sulla questione di come le foreste possano essere comprese, monitorate, modellate e gestite oggi e in futuro. La nostra ricerca collega l'ecologia forestale, la gestione forestale, il telerilevamento, il supporto decisionale, l'analisi del rischio, l'economia e gli approcci orientati agli stakeholder. Siamo fortemente coinvolti nell'insegnamento all'interno del Dipartimento di Scienze dei Sistemi Ambientali D-USYS. I nostri corsi, pratiche, attività sul campo e progetti di studenti riguardano la gestione delle risorse forestali, la pianificazione forestale e del paesaggio, l'economia forestale, il processo decisionale applicato e la gestione sostenibile dei paesaggi in condizioni ambientali mutevoli. Ci piace la ricerca rigorosa, utile, creativa e collegata al mondo reale. Lavoriamo con dati, modelli, mappe, persone, foreste, studenti e partner di scienza, pratica e amministrazione. Alcuni giorni sono circa manoscritti e codice; altri sono circa l'insegnamento, le discussioni sul campo, la scrittura della proposta, o aiutare uno studente trovare il modo migliore in avanti. Descrizione del lavoro
• Nella ricerca, svilupperai le tue idee all'interno del più ampio campo della gestione forestale ed economica, costruendo o collegando a telerilevamento, supporto decisionale e aree correlate
• Acquisirai, pulirai, analizzerai e interpreterai i dati, preparerai manoscritti scientifici, contribuirai a risultati non scientifici e presenterai il tuo lavoro a conferenze nazionali e internazionali
• Si svolgerà inoltre un ruolo attivo nello sviluppo di nuove proposte di ricerca
• Questo include unire i propri interessi scientifici con il più ampio focus di ricerca del gruppo FORM, identificare opportunità di finanziamento, contribuire a proposte come PI, collaboratore o partner, e contribuire a trasformare buone idee in progetti finanziati
• Nell'insegnamento, contribuirai a corsi esistenti e nuovi nei programmi Bachelor e Master in gestione forestale e del paesaggio, in particolare Forest Economics
• Aiuterai gli studenti a capire come le questioni ecologiche, economiche, spaziali e sociali si incontrano quando si prendono decisioni sulle foreste e sui paesaggi
• Potrai supervisionare i progetti degli studenti
• Questo include aiutare gli studenti a modellare domande di ricerca, sviluppare metodi, raccogliere e pulire i dati, applicare approcci statistici, migliorare la loro scrittura, e passare da “Ho un'idea” a “Ho una solida tesi”
• Oltre alla ricerca e all'insegnamento, sosterrai e a volte guiderai l'organizzazione di workshop, incontri, eventi e altre attività ospitate da FORM e D-USYS
• Aiuterai a mantenere e sviluppare reti scientifiche e alleanze professionali, e sarai incoraggiato a sviluppare ulteriormente le tue competenze nella gestione del progetto, supervisione, comunicazione, leadership e collaborazione Profilo
• Hai un dottorato in foresta, scienze forestali, economia forestale, scienze ambientali con una maggiore nella gestione forestale e del paesaggio, o un campo correlato, fornendo una solida conoscenza delle foreste
• Hai un forte interesse per la gestione forestale ed economia e godere di lavorare all'interfaccia della scienza, insegnarein

Chercheur postdoctoral - Gestion forestière et économie 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Vous êtes excité par les forêts, les données, l'enseignement et la grande question de savoir comment gérer les paysages forestiers sous l'incertitude? Vous aimez développer vos propres idées de recherche, travailler avec les étudiants, construire des collaborations et transformer les connaissances scientifiques en quelque chose d'utile pour la recherche, la pratique et la société? Alors cette position pourrait être pour vous. La Chaire de gestion des ressources forestières de l'ETH Zurich cherche un chercheur postdoctoral pour rejoindre notre équipe. Le poste combine recherche, enseignement, supervision des étudiants, développement de projets, et engagement avec un réseau scientifique et professionnel animé. C'est une excellente occasion pour quelqu'un qui veut grandir en tant que chercheur indépendant tout en contribuant à la recherche appliquée et tournée vers l'avenir. Le groupe FORM est une équipe de recherche dynamique et interdisciplinaire à l'ETH Zurich. Nous travaillons sur la question de savoir comment les forêts peuvent être comprises, surveillées, modélisées et gérées aujourd'hui et à l'avenir. Nos recherches relient l'écologie forestière, la gestion forestière, la télédétection, le soutien à la décision, l'analyse des risques, l'économie et les approches axées sur les intervenants. Nous sommes fortement impliqués dans l'enseignement au sein du Département de sciences des systèmes environnementaux D-USYS. Nos cours, pratiques, activités de terrain et projets étudiants couvrent la gestion des ressources forestières, la planification forestière et paysagère, l'économie forestière, la prise de décisions appliquées et la gestion durable des paysages dans des conditions environnementales changeantes. Nous aimons la recherche qui est rigoureuse, utile, créative et connectée au monde réel. Nous travaillons avec des données, des modèles, des cartes, des gens, des forêts, des étudiants et des partenaires de la science, de la pratique et de l'administration. jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Position in Ultrafast Laser Spectroscopy of Quantum Materials

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The FERROIC Lab (Laboratory for Functional Ferroic Materials) at ETH Zurich applies advanced ultrafast laser spectroscopy from the Terahertz to the ultraviolet spectral range to discover, control and understand novel quantum phenomena in condensed-matter systems. By combining state-of-the-art spectroscopy with strongly correlated electron systems, we seek to uncover fundamental physical phenomena that emerge far from equilibrium.

Our laboratory continuously develops and expands its experimental capabilities rather than relying solely on established instrumentation. We operate advanced ultrafast laser spectroscopy platforms spanning the spectral range from the Terahertz to the ultraviolet and continuously implement new experimental concepts and measurement capabilities. Our research is complemented by nonlinear optical microscopy, cryogenic experiments, atomic force microscopy, magnetic and dielectric characterization, oxide thin-film growth, and close collaboration with leading theoretical groups. We pursue fundamental experimental research while maintaining a strong connection to microscopic theory and, where appropriate, future technological opportunities.

Project background

The project investigates how intense ultrafast optical or Terahertz excitation can generate, manipulate and probe novel dynamical states in quantum materials. A central research direction is the exploration of non-Hermitian phase transitions, a recently discovered and fundamentally new class of phase transitions that emerges in the non-equilibrium dynamics of driven systems. The project aims to establish their microscopic origin, identify their universal properties and explore their manifestation across a broad range of strongly correlated materials.

More broadly, the project builds on a background of fundamental questions of ultrafast light–matter interaction in condensed-matter systems where strong electronic correlations give rise to emergent collective phenomena. Many of the materials, dynamical states and physical mechanisms under investigation remain largely unexplored, providing exceptional opportunities to discover new physical phenomena and establish new concepts in condensed-matter physics.

Job description

• You will design, build and further develop advanced ultrafast laser spectroscopy experiments operating in the optical and/or Terahertz spectral range

• Depending on your expertise and scientific interests, your research may focus predominantly on optical spectroscopy or on Terahertz spectroscopy

• You will investigate ultrafast dynamical processes on femtosecond and picosecond time scales using pump–probe techniques

• In addition to performing experiments, you will contribute to the continuous development of our experimental infrastructure and implement new measurement concepts

• This is a genuinely hands-on experimental position

• You will have primary responsibility for designing, building, optimizing and continuously extending your experimental platform, including optical alignment, troubleshooting, upgrades and routine maintenance

• We are looking for researchers who enjoy working directly with sophisticated laser systems and regard instrumentation development as an essential part of outstanding experimental physics rather than merely a prerequisite for data acquisition

• Because many of the investigated phenomena are unexplored, the project offers substantial scientific freedom

• You will have the opportunity to develop original experimental strategies, question established approaches and pursue new ideas whenever conventional solutions prove insufficient

• Close interaction with international collaborators and leading theoretical groups will complement the experimental work

Profile

• You hold (or are about to complete) a PhD in experimental physics or a closely related discipline

Posizione post-dottorale in spettroscopia laser ultraveloce dei materiali quantistici 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il FERROIC Lab (Laboratory for Functional Ferroic Materials) di ETH Zurich applica la spettroscopia laser ultraveloce avanzata del Terahertz alla gamma spettrale ultravioletta per scoprire, controllare e comprendere nuovi fenomeni quantistici nei sistemi condensati. Combinando la spettroscopia all'avanguardia con sistemi elettroni fortemente correlati, cerchiamo di scoprire fenomeni fisici fondamentali che emergono lontani dall'equilibrio. Il nostro laboratorio sviluppa e amplia continuamente le sue capacità sperimentali piuttosto che affidarsi esclusivamente alla strumentazione stabilita. Utilizziamo piattaforme di spettroscopia laser ultraveloce avanzate che spaziano dalla gamma spettrale da Terahertz all'ultravioletto e implementano continuamente nuovi concetti e capacità di misura sperimentali. La nostra ricerca è completata da microscopia ottica non lineare, esperimenti criogenici, microscopia di forza atomica, caratterizzazione magnetica e dielettrica, crescita di ossido sottile-film, e stretta collaborazione con i principali gruppi teorici. Perseguiamo la ricerca sperimentale fondamentale, pur mantenendo un forte legame con la teoria microscopica e, se del caso, future opportunità tecnologiche. Sfondo del progetto Il progetto indaga su come un'intensa eccitazione ottica ultraveloce o Terahertz possa generare, manipolare e sondare nuovi stati dinamici nei materiali quantici. Una direzione di ricerca centrale è l'esplorazione delle transizioni di fase non ermiziana, una classe di transizione di fase recentemente scoperta e fondamentalmente nuova che emerge nelle dinamiche non-equilibrio dei sistemi pilotati. Il progetto mira a stabilire la loro origine microscopica, identificare le loro proprietà universali ed esplorare la loro manifestazione attraverso una vasta gamma di materiali fortemente correlati. Più in generale, il progetto si basa su uno sfondo di questioni fondamentali di interazione ultraveloce-materia nei sistemi condensati-materia dove forti correlazioni elettroniche danno luogo a fenomeni collettivi emergenti. Molti dei materiali, stati dinamici e meccanismi fisici sotto indagine rimangono in gran parte inesplorati, fornendo opportunità eccezionali per scoprire nuovi fenomeni fisici e stabilire nuovi concetti in fisica condensata-materia. Descrizione del lavoro
• Progettare, costruire e sviluppare ulteriormente gli esperimenti avanzati di spettroscopia laser ultraveloce che operano nel campo spettrale ottico e/o Terahertz
• A seconda delle tue competenze e degli interessi scientifici, la tua ricerca può concentrarsi prevalentemente sulla spettroscopia ottica o sulla spettroscopia Terahertz
• Indagherai processi dinamici ultraveloci su scale di tempo femtosecondo e picosecondo utilizzando tecniche di pompa-probe
• Oltre a eseguire esperimenti, contribuirete allo sviluppo continuo della nostra infrastruttura sperimentale e implementare nuovi concetti di misura
• Questa è una vera e propria posizione sperimentale
• Avrete la responsabilità primaria di progettare, costruire, ottimizzare e estendere continuamente la vostra piattaforma sperimentale, tra cui allineamento ottico, risoluzione dei problemi, aggiornamenti e manutenzione ordinaria
• Siamo alla ricerca di ricercatori che amano lavorare direttamente con sistemi laser sofisticati e considerare lo sviluppo della strumentazione come parte essenziale della fisica sperimentale eccezionale piuttosto che semplicemente un prerequisito per l'acquisizione dei dati
• Poiché molti dei fenomeni indagati sono inesplorati, il progetto offre una sostanziale libertà scientifica
• Avrete l'opportunità di sviluppare strategie sperimentali originali, mettere in discussione approcci stabiliti e perseguire nuove idee ogni volta che le soluzioni convenzionali si rivelano insufficienti
• La stretta interazione con i collaboratori internazionali e i principali gruppi teorici completeranno il lavoro sperimentale Profilo
• Lei possiede (o sta per completare) un dottorato in fisica sperimentale o una disciplina strettamente correlata

descriptionByLocale.de:
Postdoc-Position in der ultraschnellen Laserspektroskopie von Quantenmaterialien 100%, Zürich, befristet Druck Druckerzeugnisse Das FERROIC Lab (Laboratory for Functional Ferroic Materials) an der ETH Zürich wendet fortschrittliche ultraschnelle Laserspektroskopie vom Terahertz bis in den ultravioletten Spektralbereich an, um neuartige Quantenphänomene in Systemen kondensierter Materie zu entdecken, zu steuern und zu verstehen. Durch die Kombination modernster Spektroskopie mit stark korrelierten Elektronensystemen versuchen wir, grundlegende physikalische Phänomene aufzudecken, die weit aus dem Gleichgewicht herauskommen. Unser Labor entwickelt und erweitert seine experimentellen Fähigkeiten kontinuierlich, anstatt sich ausschließlich auf etablierte Instrumente zu verlassen. Wir betreiben fortschrittliche ultraschnelle Laserspektroskopieplattformen, die den Spektralbereich vom Terahertz bis zum Ultraviolett abdecken und kontinuierlich neue experimentelle Konzepte und Messmöglichkeiten implementieren. Unsere Forschung wird ergänzt durch nichtlineare optische Mikroskopie, kryogene Experimente, Rasterkraftmikroskopie, magnetische und dielektrische Charakterisierung, Oxiddünnfilmwachstum und enge Zusammenarbeit mit führenden theoretischen Gruppen. Wir verfolgen grundlegende experimentelle Forschung unter Beibehaltung einer starken Verbindung zur mikroskopischen Theorie und gegebenenfalls zu zukünftigen technologischen Möglichkeiten. Projekthintergrund Das Projekt untersucht, wie intensive ultraschnelle optische oder Terahertz-Anregung neue dynamische Zustände in Quantenmaterialien erzeugen, manipulieren und untersuchen kann. Eine zentrale Forschungsrichtung ist die Erforschung nicht-hermitischer Phasenübergänge, einer kürzlich entdeckten und grundlegend neuen Klasse von Phasenübergängen, die in der Nichtgleichgewichtsdynamik angetriebener Systeme entsteht. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, ihren mikroskopischen Ursprung zu ermitteln, ihre universellen Eigenschaften zu identifizieren und ihre Manifestation in einem breiten Spektrum stark korrelierter Materialien zu erforschen. Im weiteren Sinne baut das Projekt auf einem Hintergrund grundlegender Fragen der ultraschnellen Licht-Materie-Wechselwirkung in Systemen kondensierter Materie auf, in denen starke elektronische Korrelationen zu kollektiven Phänomenen führen. Viele der untersuchten Materialien, dynamischen Zustände und physikalischen Mechanismen bleiben weitgehend unerforscht und bieten außergewöhnliche Möglichkeiten, neue physikalische Phänomene zu entdecken und neue Konzepte in der Physik der kondensierten Materie zu etablieren. Stellenbeschreibung
• Sie entwerfen, bauen und entwickeln fortschrittliche ultraschnelle Laserspektroskopie-Experimente, die im optischen und / oder Terahertz-Spektralbereich arbeiten
• Abhängig von Ihrer Expertise und Ihren wissenschaftlichen Interessen kann sich Ihre Forschung hauptsächlich auf die optische Spektroskopie oder die Terahertz-Spektroskopie konzentrieren.
• Sie untersuchen ultraschnelle dynamische Prozesse auf Femtosekunden- und Pikosekunden-Zeitskalen mit Pump-Probe-Techniken
• Neben der Durchführung von Experimenten tragen Sie zur kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung unserer experimentellen Infrastruktur bei und implementieren neue Messkonzepte
• Dies ist eine wirklich praktische experimentelle Position
• Sie tragen die Hauptverantwortung für die Gestaltung, den Aufbau, die Optimierung und die kontinuierliche Erweiterung Ihrer experimentellen Plattform, einschließlich optischer Ausrichtung, Fehlerbehebung, Upgrades und routinemäßiger Wartung.
• Wir suchen Forscher, die gerne direkt mit anspruchsvollen Lasersystemen arbeiten und die Instrumentenentwicklung als wesentlichen Bestandteil herausragender experimenteller Physik und nicht nur als Voraussetzung für die Datenerfassung betrachten.
• Da viele der untersuchten Phänomene unerforscht sind, bietet das Projekt erhebliche wissenschaftliche Freiheit.
• Sie haben die Möglichkeit, originelle experimentelle Strategien zu entwickeln, etablierte Ansätze zu hinterfragen und neue Ideen zu verfolgen, wenn sich herkömmliche Lösungen als unzureichend erweisen.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Position postdoctorale en spectroscopie laser ultrarapide des matériaux quantiques 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le laboratoire FERROIC (Laboratory for Functional Ferroic Materials) de l'ETH Zurich applique la spectroscopie laser ultrarapide avancée du Térahertz à la gamme spectrale ultraviolette pour découvrir, contrôler et comprendre de nouveaux phénomènes quantiques dans les systèmes de matière condensée. En combinant la spectroscopie de pointe avec des systèmes électroniques fortement corrélés, nous cherchons à découvrir des phénomènes physiques fondamentaux qui émergent loin de l'équilibre. Notre laboratoire développe et développe en permanence ses capacités expérimentales plutôt que de s'appuyer uniquement sur des instruments établis. Nous exploitons des plates-formes de spectroscopie laser ultrarapide de pointe couvrant la gamme spectrale du Térahertz aux ultraviolets et implémentons continuellement de nouveaux concepts expérimentaux et de nouvelles capacités de mesure. Notre recherche est complétée par la microscopie optique non linéaire, des expériences cryogéniques, la microscopie de force atomique, la caractérisation magnétique et diélectrique, la croissance du film mince d'oxyde et une collaboration étroite avec les principaux groupes théoriques. Nous poursuivons la recherche expérimentale fondamentale tout en maintenant un lien solide avec la théorie microscopique et, le cas échéant, les possibilités technologiques futures. Contexte du projet Le projet étudie comment l'excitation ultrarapide ou Térahertz peut générer, manipuler et sonder de nouveaux états dynamiques dans les matériaux quantiques. Une direction centrale de la recherche est l'exploration de transitions de phase non-Hermitienne, une classe de transitions de phase récemment découverte et fondamentalement nouvelle qui émerge dans la dynamique de non-équilibre des systèmes entraînés. Le projet vise à établir leur origine microscopique, à identifier leurs propriétés universelles et à explorer leur manifestation sur un large éventail de matériaux fortement corrélés. De manière plus générale, le projet s'appuie sur un contexte de questions fondamentales concernant l'interaction entre la lumière et la matière ultrarapide dans les systèmes de matière condensée où de fortes corrélations électroniques donnent lieu à des phénomènes collectifs émergents. Beaucoup de matériaux, d'états dynamiques et de mécanismes physiques à l'étude restent largement inexplorés, offrant des possibilités exceptionnelles de découvrir de nouveaux phénomènes physiques et d'établir de nouveaux concepts en physique de la matière condensée. Description du poste
• Vous allez concevoir, construire et développer des expériences avancées de spectroscopie laser ultrarapide opérant dans la gamme spectrale optique et/ou Térahertz
• Selon votre expertise et vos intérêts scientifiques, votre recherche peut se concentrer principalement sur la spectroscopie optique ou la spectroscopie Térahertz
• Vous étudierez les processus dynamiques ultrarapides sur les échelles de temps femtoseconde et picoseconde en utilisant des techniques de sonde-pompe
• En plus de réaliser des expériences, vous contribuerez au développement continu de notre infrastructure expérimentale et mettre en œuvre de nouveaux concepts de mesure
• C'est vraiment une position expérimentale pratique
• Vous aurez la responsabilité première de concevoir, de construire, d'optimiser et d'étendre continuellement votre plateforme expérimentale, y compris l'alignement optique, le dépannage, les mises à niveau et l'entretien de routine
• Nous recherchons des chercheurs qui aiment travailler directement avec des systèmes laser sophistiqués et considérer le développement de l'instrumentation comme un élément essentiel de la physique expérimentale exceptionnelle plutôt que simplement une condition préalable à l'acquisition de données
• Comme bon nombre des phénomènes étudiés sont inexplorés, le projet offre une liberté scientifique substantielle
• Vous aurez la possibilité de développer des stratégies expérimentales originales, de questionner des approches établies et de poursuivre de nouvelles idées chaque fois que les solutions conventionnelles s'avéreront insuffisantes

jobs.description:
PhD Positions in Neurotechnology: Next Generation Non-invasive Neurotechnologies & Brain Therapies

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Neurotechnology Group of Prof. Mehmet Fatih Yanik at ETH Zurich is recruiting outstanding PhD students to join a newly funded LOOP Zurich Flagship Project focused on advancing a breakthrough technology to clinic for non-invasive targeted drug delivery to the brain. Our laboratory recently developed a novel focused ultrasound-mediated targeted drug delivery platform, published in Nature Communications , that enables localized, hyper-efficient delivery of therapeutic compounds to specific brain regions without invasive surgery.

Project background

We develop advanced focused ultrasound technologies, adaptive closed-loop control algorithms, and ultrasound-responsive micro/nano therapeutic carriers as an integrated precision drug delivery platform for the brain. Our approach employs a novel two-component ultrasound strategy that first concentrates drug carriers within the target region and subsequently triggers localized drug release, achieving high therapeutic concentrations exclusively at the desired site while minimizing systemic exposure. To ensure safe, precise, and reproducible therapy, the platform continuously monitors acoustic emissions from carriers, automatically adjusts ultrasound exposure in real time, and preserves blood–brain barrier integrity. By integrating therapeutic carrier design, robotics, medical imaging, real-time sensing, and intelligent control into a unified system, this technology establishes a new paradigm for precision neurotherapeutics and opens new opportunities for treating epilepsy, brain tumors, neurodegenerative diseases, psychiatric disorders, and other neurological disorders. The long-term goal of this project is to establish this technology as a clinically applicable therapeutic platform by integrating targeted drug delivery with advanced neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and closed-loop neuromodulation. The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance this technology from proof-of-concept toward clinical translation. Successful candidates will further develop the technology, investigate its therapeutic potential for neurological disorders, perform preclinical validation in rodent and large-animal models, and contribute to the preparation of first-in-human clinical studies. The project is conducted in close collaboration with Swiss Epilepsy Clinic Lengg, the Department of Neurosurgery at University Hospital Zurich, and the Vetsuisse Faculty of the University of Zurich.

Job description

The successful candidate will play a central role in the development and translation of our focused ultrasound-mediated targeted drug delivery platform.

Depending on experience and interests, the project may include:

• Development of next-generation focused ultrasound systems

• fMRI-guided treatment planning and targeting

• Optimization of targeted drug delivery and therapeutic dosing

• Development of closed-loop ultrasound neuromodulation systems

• Design of custom hardware and software

• Electrophysiology and multimodal neurophysiology

• Rodent and large-animal neuroscience experiments

• Translation of the technology toward clinical application

• Collaboration with clinicians to prepare first-in-human clinical studies

• Medical device development and regulatory approval

This is a highly interdisciplinary project at the interface of neuroscience, biomedical engineering, physics, electrical engineering, medical imaging, robotics, and translational medicine.

Profile

We are looking for highly motivated and creative researchers who enjoy solving challenging interdisciplinary problems.

Applicants should hold a Master’s degree in one of the following disciplines:

• Biomedical Engineering

• Electrical Engineering

• Mechanical Engineering

• Physics

• Neuroscience

• Computer Science

• Chemistry

• or a closely related field

PhD Posizioni in Neurotecnologie: Prossima Generazione Neurotecnologie non invasive & Terapie cerebrali 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Gruppo di Neurotecnologie del Prof. Mehmet Fatih Yanik all'ETH di Zurigo sta reclutando studenti di dottorato eccezionali per aderire a un progetto di bandierina LOOP di Zurigo recentemente finanziato, mirato a promuovere una tecnologia di innovazione per la clinica per la consegna non invasiva di droga mirata al cervello. Il nostro laboratorio ha recentemente sviluppato una nuova piattaforma di distribuzione mirata di farmaci ultrasuoni, pubblicata in Nature Communications , che consente la consegna localizzata e iper-efficiente di composti terapeutici a specifiche regioni cerebrali senza chirurgia invasiva. Sfondo del progetto Sviluppiamo tecnologie avanzate di ultrasuoni focalizzate, algoritmi di controllo a ciclo chiuso adattativi e portanti terapeutici micro/nano ad ultrasuoni ad ultrasuoni come piattaforma integrata di distribuzione di farmaci di precisione per il cervello. Il nostro approccio impiega una nuova strategia a due componenti ad ultrasuoni che concentra prima i portatori di droga all'interno della regione di destinazione e in seguito innesca il rilascio localizzato di droga, raggiungendo alte concentrazioni terapeutiche esclusivamente al sito desiderato, riducendo al minimo l'esposizione sistemica. Per garantire una terapia sicura, precisa e riproducibile, la piattaforma monitora continuamente le emissioni acustiche dei vettori, regola automaticamente l'esposizione agli ultrasuoni in tempo reale e preserva l'integrità della barriera emato-encefalica. Integrando il design del vettore terapeutico, la robotica, l'imaging medico, il rilevamento in tempo reale e il controllo intelligente in un sistema unificato, questa tecnologia stabilisce un nuovo paradigma per i neuroterapeutici di precisione e apre nuove opportunità per il trattamento dell'epilessia, dei tumori cerebrali, delle malattie neurodegenerative, dei disturbi psichiatrici e di altri disturbi neurologici. L'obiettivo a lungo termine di questo progetto è quello di stabilire questa tecnologia come una piattaforma terapeutica clinicamente applicabile integrando la fornitura di farmaci mirati con neuroimaging avanzato, elettrofisiologia e neuromodulazione a ciclo chiuso. L'obiettivo primario di questo progetto di dottorato è quello di avanzare questa tecnologia dalla prova di concetto verso la traduzione clinica. I candidati di successo svilupperanno ulteriormente la tecnologia, studieranno il suo potenziale terapeutico per i disturbi neurologici, eseguiranno la validazione preclinica nei modelli roditori e di grandi animali, e contribuiranno alla preparazione di studi clinici di primo in-umani. Il progetto è condotto in stretta collaborazione con la clinica svizzera di epilessia Lengg, il Dipartimento di neurochirurgia presso l'ospedale universitario di Zurigo, e la Facoltà di Vetsuisse dell'Università di Zurigo. PhD Positions in Neurotechnology: Next Generation Non-invasive Neurotechnologies & Brain Therapies

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Neurotechnology Group of Prof. Mehmet Fatih Yanik at ETH Zurich is recruiting outstanding PhD students to join a newly funded LOOP Zurich Flagship Project focused on advancing a breakthrough technology to clinic for non-invasive targeted drug delivery to the brain. Our laboratory recently developed a novel focused ultrasound-mediated targeted drug delivery platform, published in Nature Communications , that enables localized, hyper-efficient delivery of therapeutic compounds to specific brain regions without invasive surgery.

Project background

We develop advanced focused ultrasound technologies, adaptive closed-loop control algorithms, and ultrasound-responsive micro/nano therapeutic carriers as an integrated precision drug delivery platform for the brain. Our approach employs a novel two-component ultrasound strategy that first concentrates drug carriers within the target region and subsequently triggers localized drug release, achieving high therapeutic concentrations exclusively at the desired site while minimizing systemic exposure. To ensure safe, precise, and reproducible therapy, the platform continuously monitors acoustic emissions from carriers, automatically adjusts ultrasound exposure in real time, and preserves blood–brain barrier integrity. By integrating therapeutic carrier design, robotics, medical imaging, real-time sensing, and intelligent control into a unified system, this technology establishes a new paradigm for precision neurotherapeutics and opens new opportunities for treating epilepsy, brain tumors, neurodegenerative diseases, psychiatric disorders, and other neurological disorders. The long-term goal of this project is to establish this technology as a clinically applicable therapeutic platform by integrating targeted drug delivery with advanced neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and closed-loop neuromodulation. The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance this technology from proof-of-concept toward clinical translation. Successful candidates will further develop the technology, investigate its therapeutic potential for neurological disorders, perform preclinical validation in rodent and large-animal models, and contribute to the preparation of first-in-human clinical studies. The project is conducted in close collaboration with Swiss Epilepsy Clinic Lengg, the Department of Neurosurgery at University Hospital Zurich, and the Vetsuisse Faculty of the University of Zurich.

Job description

The successful candidate will play a central role in the development and translation of our focused ultrasound-mediated targeted drug delivery platform.

Depending on experience and interests, the project may include:

• Development of next-generation focused ultrasound systems

• fMRI-guided treatment planning and targeting

• Optimization of targeted drug delivery and therapeutic dosing

• Development of closed-loop ultrasound neuromodulation systems

• Design of custom hardware and software

• Electrophysiology and multimodal neurophysiology

• Rodent and large-animal neuroscience experiments

• Translation of the technology toward clinical application

• Collaboration with clinicians to prepare first-in-human clinical studies

• Medical device development and regulatory approval

This is a highly interdisciplinary project at the interface of neuroscience, biomedical engineering, physics, electrical engineering, medical imaging, robotics, and translational medicine.

Profile

We are looking for highly motivated and creative researchers who enjoy solving challenging interdisciplinary problems.

Applicants should hold a Master’s degree in one of the following disciplines:

• Biomedical Engineering

• Electrical Engineering

• Mechanical Engineering

• Physics

• Neuroscience

• Computer Science

• Chemistry

• or a closely related field

PhD Positionen in der Neurotechnologie: Next Generation Nicht-invasive Neurotechnologien & Gehirntherapien 100%, Zürich, befristet Druck Druckerzeugnisse Die Neurotechnologie-Gruppe von Prof. Mehmet Fatih Yanik an der ETH Zürich rekrutiert herausragende Doktoranden für ein neu finanziertes LOOP Zurich Flagship Project, das sich darauf konzentriert, eine bahnbrechende Technologie für die nicht-invasive gezielte Medikamentenabgabe an das Gehirn in der Klinik voranzutreiben. Unser Labor hat vor kurzem eine neuartige fokussierte Ultraschall-vermittelte zielgerichtete Medikamentenverabreichungsplattform entwickelt, die in Nature Communications veröffentlicht wurde und eine lokalisierte, hypereffiziente Verabreichung therapeutischer Verbindungen in bestimmte Hirnregionen ohne invasive Chirurgie ermöglicht. Projekthintergrund Wir entwickeln fortschrittliche fokussierte Ultraschalltechnologien, adaptive Regelalgorithmen und ultraschallresponsive mikro-/nanotherapeutische Träger als integrierte Plattform für die Verabreichung von Präzisionsmedikamenten für das Gehirn. Unser Ansatz verwendet eine neuartige Zwei-Komponenten-Ultraschallstrategie, die zunächst Arzneimittelträger in der Zielregion konzentriert und anschließend eine lokalisierte Arzneimittelfreisetzung auslöst, wodurch hohe therapeutische Konzentrationen ausschließlich an der gewünschten Stelle erreicht und gleichzeitig die systemische Exposition minimiert wird. Um eine sichere, präzise und reproduzierbare Therapie zu gewährleisten, überwacht die Plattform kontinuierlich die akustischen Emissionen von Trägern, passt die Ultraschallbelastung automatisch in Echtzeit an und bewahrt die Integrität der Blut-Hirn-Schranke. Durch die Integration von therapeutischem Trägerdesign, Robotik, medizinischer Bildgebung, Echtzeiterfassung und intelligenter Steuerung in ein einheitliches System etabliert diese Technologie ein neues Paradigma für Präzisions-Neurotherapeutika und eröffnet neue Möglichkeiten zur Behandlung von Epilepsie, Hirntumoren, neurodegenerativen Erkrankungen, psychiatrischen Störungen und anderen neurologischen Störungen. Langfristiges Ziel dieses Projekts ist es, diese Technologie als klinisch anwendbare therapeutische Plattform zu etablieren, indem eine gezielte Wirkstoffabgabe mit fortschrittlicher Neuroimaging-, Elektrophysiologie- und Closed-Loop-Neuromodulation integriert wird. Das primäre Ziel dieses PhD-Projekts ist es, diese Technologie vom Proof-of-Concept hin zur klinischen Übersetzung voranzutreiben. Erfolgreiche Kandidaten werden die Technologie weiterentwickeln, ihr therapeutisches Potenzial für neurologische Erkrankungen untersuchen, präklinische Validierungen an Nager- und Großtiermodellen durchführen und zur Vorbereitung von klinischen Erststudien am Menschen beitragen. Das Projekt wird in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Schweizerischen Epilepsieklinik Lengg, der Abteilung für Neurochirurgie am Universitätsklinikum Zürich und der Vetsuisse-Fakultät der Universität Zürich durchgeführt. Stellenbeschreibung Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird eine zentrale Rolle bei der Entwicklung und Übersetzung unserer fokussierten ultraschallvermittelten zielgerichteten Medikamentenverabreichungsplattform spielen. • Zusammenarbeit mit Klinikern zur Vorbereitung erster klinischer Studien am Menschen

Postes de doctorat en neurotechnologie : neurotechnologies et thérapies cérébrales non envahissantes de la prochaine génération 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Groupe Neurotechnologie du Prof. Mehmet Fatih Yanik à l'ETH Zurich recrute d'excellents doctorants pour rejoindre un nouveau projet phare de LOOP Zurich axé sur la promotion d'une technologie de pointe à la clinique pour la livraison de médicaments ciblés non invasifs au cerveau. Notre laboratoire a récemment mis au point une nouvelle plate-forme de livraison ciblée par ultrasons, publiée dans Nature Communications , qui permet une livraison localisée et hyper efficace de composés thérapeutiques dans certaines régions du cerveau sans chirurgie invasive. Contexte du projet Nous développons des technologies d'échographie ciblées de pointe, des algorithmes adaptatifs de contrôle en boucle fermée et des porteuses micro/nano-thérapeutiques réceptives aux ultrasons comme plate-forme intégrée de livraison de médicaments de précision pour le cerveau. Notre approche repose sur une nouvelle stratégie d'échographie bicomposante qui concentre d'abord les porteurs de médicaments dans la région cible et déclenche par la suite la libération localisée de médicaments, atteignant des concentrations thérapeutiques élevées exclusivement au site désiré tout en minimisant l'exposition systémique. Afin d'assurer une thérapie sûre, précise et reproductible, la plateforme surveille en permanence les émissions acoustiques des porteurs, ajuste automatiquement l'exposition aux ultrasons en temps réel et préserve l'intégrité de la barrière hémato-encéphalique. En intégrant la conception de supports thérapeutiques, la robotique, l'imagerie médicale, la détection en temps réel et le contrôle intelligent dans un système unifié, cette technologie établit un nouveau paradigme pour la neurothérapeutique de précision et ouvre de nouvelles possibilités de traitement de l'épilepsie, des tumeurs cérébrales, des maladies neurodégénératives, des troubles psychiatriques et d'autres troubles neurologiques. L'objectif à long terme de ce projet est d'établir cette technologie comme une plateforme thérapeutique cliniquement applicable en intégrant la livraison ciblée de médicaments avec neuroimagerie avancée, électrophysiologie et neuromodulation en boucle fermée. L'objectif principal de ce projet de doctorat est de faire progresser cette technologie de la preuve de concept vers la traduction clinique. Les candidats retenus développeront davantage la technologie, étudieront son potentiel thérapeutique pour les troubles neurologiques, effectueront une validation préclinique chez les rongeurs et les grands animaux et contribueront à la préparation d'études cliniques sur le premier patient. Le projet est mené en étroite collaboration avec la Clinique suisse d'épilepsie Lengg, le Département de neurochirurgie de l'hôpital universitaire de Zurich et la Faculté Vetsuisse de l'Université de Zurich. Description du poste Le candidat retenu jouera un rôle central dans l'élaboration et la traduction de notre plateforme ciblée de distribution de médicaments par ultrasons. Selon l'expérience et les intérêts, le projet peut comprendre :
• Développement de systèmes d'échographie de prochaine génération
• Planification et ciblage des traitements guidés par l'IRMf
• Optimisation de l'administration ciblée de médicaments et du dosage thérapeutique
• Développement de systèmes de neuromodulation à ultrasons en boucle fermée
• Conception de matériel et de logiciels personnalisés
• Électrophysiologie et neurophysiologie multimodale
• Expériences de neurosciences rodentes et de neurosciences des grands animaux
• Traduction de la technologie vers l'application clinique
• Collaboration avec les cliniciens pour préparer les premières études cliniques sur l'humain
• Développement d'instruments médicaux et approbation réglementaire Il s'agit d'un projet hautement interdisciplinaire à l'interface des neurosciences, génie biomédical, physique, génie électrique, imagerie médicale, robotique et médecine translationnelle. Profil Nous recherchons des chercheurs hautement motivés et créatifs qui aiment résoudre des problèmes interdisciplinaires difficiles. Les candidats doivent être titulaires d'une maîtrise dans l'une des disciplines suivantes :
• Génie biomédical

80%-100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Die ETH Zürich startet mit dem «Living Lab HIL» ein pionierhaftes Forschungsprojekt mit direktem Bezug zur Baupraxis. Das HIL-Gebäude auf dem Campus Hönggerberg wird zu einem Reallabor. Der sanierungsbedürftige Bau wird umgebaut und erweitert. In den kommenden Jahren erforschen und planen Professuren der Departemente Architektur (D-ARCH) sowie Bau, Umwelt und Geomatik (D-BAUG) die Sanierung des Gebäudes HIL im Sinne des zirkulären Bauens. Ziel ist es, das nachhaltige Entwerfen und Bauen im Bestand weiterzuentwickeln und exemplarisch an einem realen Planungs- und Bauprojekt anzuwenden. Koordiniert und entwickelt wird das Projekt vom Living Lab HIL Projektteam.

Zur wissenschaftlichen Begleitung des Living Lab HIL Projekts suchen wir eine forschungserfahrene Persönlichkeit mit Expertise in den Bereichen Architektur, Nachhaltigkeit und Digitalisierung. Ihr Ziel ist es aktuelle Forschungserkenntnisse wirkungsvoll in die Praxis zu übertragen. Zudem sind Sie für Kollaborationen mit Industriepartnern und ETH-Spin-Offs zuständig. Ergänzend zur Projektkommunikation koordinieren Sie wissenschaftliche Publikationen und tragen so massgeblich zur akademischen Sichtbarkeit des Living Lab HIL bei.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Forschungskollaboration: Inhaltliche und organisatorische Begleitung der wissenschaftlichen Kollaborationen («Input-Projekte») in enger Abstimmung mit den Professuren

• Industriekollaboration: Strategische Schnittstelle und Koordination der Zusammenarbeit mit Industriepartnern und ETH-Spin-Offs

• Förderpartnerschaften: Aktive Zusammenarbeit mit der ETH Foundation zum Aufbau von Förderpartnerschaften zur Akquise von Fördergeldern

• Wissenschaftliche Publikationen: Koordination und inhaltliche Mitarbeit an kollaborativen wissenschaftlichen Publikationen (Papers, Fachartikel und Forschungsberichte)

• Koordination: aktive interne Abstimmung mit der Leitung «Input Projekte»

Profil

• Forschungsausweis: Nachgewiesene Publikationsleistung (Peer-Reviewed) und Erfahrung in der Verfassung wissenschaftlicher Texte auf internationalem Niveau

Research Intern – Machine learning and digital twins

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

inspire AG is the leading Swiss competence centre for product innovation and advanced manufacturing.
As a strategic partner of ETH Zurich, our mission is to transfer knowledge and technology
from research to Swiss machine, electrical and metal industries.
The research group Control and Automation at inspire AG offers the following position in collaboration
with an industry partner.

Project background

Our research group works on increasing the efficiency of robotics systems in real-world deployment
by enabling quick data collection, calibration, and policy training while ensuring safety and efficiency.
For this, we develop novel learning-based control and policy optimization techniques.
We're looking for a skilled machine learning (ML) engineer to develop cutting-edge AI algorithms for
digital twin applications in real-world industrial systems. The digital twin applications will include process
monitoring, estimation, analysis, optimization, and control policy development. The project requires
hands-on expertise in ML, time-series forecasting, modelling, and control of industrial plants.

Job description

• Develop customized Digital Twins for industrial applications using ML from real data

• Develop and maintain the codebase to support various training modules and libraries

• Collaborate with our industrial partner and collect extensive datasets on real hardware

• Design and deploy control policy on industrial applications

Profile

Required experience

• Pursuing a master’s degree (university) in robotics, electrical or mechanical engineering, or CS.

• Practical knowledge of time series modelling, seq2seq, and data-driven digital twin models (e.g.,

• Transformers, Mamba, LSTMs) with applications in industry.

• Knowledge/courses taken on estimation theory, network modeling, and graph theory are a plus.

• Excellent coding skills in python, ROS, and ML pipeline experience on simulator and training libraries.

• Good foundation in linear algebra, numerical methods, optimization, and control theory.

• An excellent knowledge (written/oral) of English is a must. Knowledge of German is beneficial.
Required people skills

• Highly self-organized and structured way of working and solution orientation.

• High motivation and willingness to learn new skills.

• High level of teamwork, positive work attitude and creativity.

Workplace

We offer

We offer an internship position in our group, Control and Automation at inspire AG. Through the close
cooperation with our project partner, you will quickly establish contacts to industry. In our young team
you will work at the forefront of today's knowledge in industrial AI/ML.

Curious? So are we.

Come partner strategico dell'ETH Zurigo, la nostra missione è quella di trasferire conoscenza e tecnologia dalla ricerca alle industrie della macchina svizzera, dell'elettricità e dei metalli. Il gruppo di ricerca Control and Automation at ispira AG offre la seguente posizione in collaborazione con un partner del settore. Sfondo del progetto Il nostro gruppo di ricerca lavora per aumentare l'efficienza dei sistemi robotici nella distribuzione del mondo reale consentendo una rapida raccolta dei dati, calibrazione e formazione politica, garantendo al contempo sicurezza ed efficienza. Per questo, sviluppiamo nuove tecniche di controllo e ottimizzazione delle politiche basate sull'apprendimento. Stiamo cercando un ingegnere esperto di machine learning (ML) per sviluppare algoritmi AI all'avanguardia per applicazioni digitali gemellate in sistemi industriali reali. Le applicazioni gemelle digitali includono il processo monitoraggio, stima, analisi, ottimizzazione e sviluppo della politica di controllo. Il progetto richiede competenze pratiche in ML, previsioni di tempo, modellazione e controllo di impianti industriali. Descrizione del lavoro
• Sviluppare gemelli digitali personalizzati per applicazioni industriali utilizzando ML da dati reali
• Sviluppare e mantenere la base di codice per supportare vari moduli di formazione e biblioteche
• Collabora con il nostro partner industriale e raccogli numerosi set di dati su hardware reale
• Progettazione e distribuzione della politica di controllo sulle applicazioni industriali Profilo Esperienza richiesta
• A seguito di un master (università) in robotica, ingegneria elettrica o meccanica, o CS.
• Conoscenza pratica della modellazione delle serie temporali, seq2seq, e modelli gemellari digitali basati sui dati (ad esempio,
• Trasformatori, Mamba, LSTM) con applicazioni nell'industria.
• Conoscenza / corsi presi sulla teoria della stima, la modellazione della rete e la teoria dei grafici sono un plus.
• Eccellenti capacità di codifica in python, ROS e ML esperienza di pipeline su librerie di simulazione e formazione.
• Buona fondazione in algebra lineare, metodi numerici, ottimizzazione e teoria del controllo.
• Una conoscenza eccellente (scritta/orale) dell'inglese è un must. La conoscenza del tedesco è benefica. Capacità necessarie delle persone
• Altamente auto-organizzato e strutturato modo di lavoro e orientamento della soluzione.
• Alta motivazione e disponibilità ad imparare nuove competenze.
• Alto livello di lavoro di squadra, atteggiamento di lavoro positivo e creatività. Attraverso la chiusura cooperazione con il nostro partner di progetto, si istituirà rapidamente i contatti all'industria. Nella nostra giovane squadra lavorerai all'avanguardia della conoscenza di oggi in AI/ML industriale. Curioso? Anche noi. jobs.description:
PhD Position in NCCR Genesis: On the rise of molecular complexity at the Origin of Life

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Open PhD position in NCCR Genesis: On the rise of molecular complexity at the Origin of Life
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe.

Project background

This interdisciplinary research infrastructure of the NCCR Genesis brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct on-site measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Further details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch .

Job description

The successful candidate will investigate the emergence of molecular complexity from simple building blocks, such as amino acids and nucleotides, toward self-replicating chemical systems. The project will focus on peptide amyloids and their interactions with RNA and membranes, with the long-term goal of understanding the emergence of proto-ribosomal machinery.

Starting date: Fall 2026 or by mutual agreement. There is no deadline and the position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

The PhD candidate will join the Riek Group at ETH Zurich , within the Institute of Molecular Physical Science, Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences (D-CHAB).

Profile

• Applicants with a Master's degree should have a strong background in experimental chemistry, ideally with experience in physical and/or organic chemistry, and a keen interest in interdisciplinary research.

• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere.

• Fluent communication skills (written and presentation) in English are essential.

Workplace

We offer

• A fully funded PhD position for approximately four years at a world-leading university, offering an outstanding scientific and collaborative research environment.

• As part of an enthusiastic and interdisciplinary team, you will engage in cutting-edge research with access to state-of-the-art laboratories and experimental facilities. The position supports the development of critical thinking, data analysis, problem-solving, and project management skills while providing opportunities to publish in leading journals and present at international conferences.

• You can also expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits , and ETH Zürich is actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. PhD Position in NCCR Genesis: On the rise of molecular complexity at the Origin of Life

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Open PhD position in NCCR Genesis: On the rise of molecular complexity at the Origin of Life
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe.

Project background

This interdisciplinary research infrastructure of the NCCR Genesis brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct on-site measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Further details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch .

Job description

The successful candidate will investigate the emergence of molecular complexity from simple building blocks, such as amino acids and nucleotides, toward self-replicating chemical systems. The project will focus on peptide amyloids and their interactions with RNA and membranes, with the long-term goal of understanding the emergence of proto-ribosomal machinery.

Starting date: Fall 2026 or by mutual agreement. There is no deadline and the position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

The PhD candidate will join the Riek Group at ETH Zurich , within the Institute of Molecular Physical Science, Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences (D-CHAB).

Profile

• Applicants with a Master's degree should have a strong background in experimental chemistry, ideally with experience in physical and/or organic chemistry, and a keen interest in interdisciplinary research.

• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere.

• Fluent communication skills (written and presentation) in English are essential.

Workplace

We offer

• A fully funded PhD position for approximately four years at a world-leading university, offering an outstanding scientific and collaborative research environment.

• As part of an enthusiastic and interdisciplinary team, you will engage in cutting-edge research with access to state-of-the-art laboratories and experimental facilities. The position supports the development of critical thinking, data analysis, problem-solving, and project management skills while providing opportunities to publish in leading journals and present at international conferences.

• You can also expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits , and ETH Zürich is actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. jobs.description:
PhD Position in Cryogenic Carbonate Mineralization and Carbon Dioxide Fluxes

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Geomitigation of Greenhouse Gases group at ETH Zürich is actively recruiting a highly motivated and creative PhD candidate with a strong interest in low temperature experimental geochemistry. The position is part of a newly funded project at the intersection of experimental geochemistry, cryosphere science, and planetary surface processes. The position is fully funded for 4 years, with an expected start date of 4 January 2027.

Project background

In this role, you will investigate how freezing influences carbonate mineral formation and carbon dioxide exchange under conditions simulating cryogenic environments such as glaciers, sea ice, permafrost, and ice-rich planetary systems. You will help contribute to a new experimental platform for low-temperature geochemistry at ETH Zurich and engage in an emerging research direction focused on how ice formation influences carbon cycling in cold environments. The project combines controlled freezing experiments, aqueous geochemistry, gas monitoring, and mineral characterization to develop a process-based framework for understanding when freezing promotes carbon release, carbon storage, or both.

Job description

• Lead and execute controlled cryogenic laboratory experiments using customized freezing and thawing reactor systems.

• Measure and interpret liquid and gas geochemical data using a variety of analytical instrumentation ( e.g. , Gas analyzers, HPIC, ICP-OES, UVVis-Spectroscopy, Potentiometric Titration).

• Recover and characterize carbonate minerals formed during freezing using mineralogical and microscopic technique.

• Develop and parameterize a predictive kinetic framework using time-resolved geochemical measurements.

• Synthesize experimental datasets and disseminate findings through scientific manuscripts.

• Present your research at international conferences and workshops.

• Collaborate closely with the Principal Investigator, a postdoctoral researcher, and other group members while contributing to a supportive and communicative group culture.

Profile

We are looking for a candidate that is curious, careful, and motivated by experimental research. You enjoy working with complex geochemical systems and are excited by the challenge of developing new methods and datasets.

• An MSc degree in geochemistry, Earth sciences, environmental chemistry, chemistry, or a closely related discipline.

• A strong interest or background in low-temperature geochemistry, water-rock interactions, mineral formation, carbonate and aqueous redox chemistry, cryosphere science, or related fields.

• Motivation for hands-on laboratory work and experimental troubleshooting.

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to work carefully with quantitative chemical data.

• Creativity, resilience, and independence when working on exploratory research questions.

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

• Excellent spoken and written English.

Experience with reactive-transport/geochemical modeling is beneficial but not required.

Workplace

We offer

• A collaborative research environment: You will join an enthusiastic, inclusive, and highly collaborative research group where high quality research, open discussion, and creative scientific thinking are strongly valued. You will benefit from a dynamic departmental setting with broad expertise, excellent research infrastructure, and opportunities for interdisciplinary exchange.

• Mentorship and career development: You will receive direct mentorship from the PI and senior members of the group along with support in developing your skills in experimental design, data interpretation, scientific writing, and academic framework development. You will participate in the broader academic community through publications and presentations at scientific conferenc

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione del PhD in Carbonato criogenico Mineralizzazione e Flussi di anidride carbonica 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il gruppo Geomitigation of Greenhouse Gases di ETH Zürich sta reclutando attivamente un candidato di dottorato altamente motivato e creativo con un forte interesse nella geochimica sperimentale a bassa temperatura. La posizione fa parte di un progetto appena finanziato all'incrocio tra geochimica sperimentale, scienza della criosfera e processi superficiali planetari. La posizione è completamente finanziata per 4 anni, con una data di inizio prevista del 4 gennaio 2027. Sfondo del progetto In questo ruolo, si indaga su come il congelamento influenza la formazione di minerali carbonati e lo scambio di anidride carbonica in condizioni simulando ambienti criogenici come ghiacciai, ghiaccio marino, permafrost e sistemi planetari ricchi di ghiaccio. Contribuirai ad una nuova piattaforma sperimentale per la geochimica a bassa temperatura presso l'ETH di Zurigo e ad impegnarsi in una direzione di ricerca emergente focalizzata su come la formazione del ghiaccio influenza il ciclismo al carbonio in ambienti freddi. Il progetto combina esperimenti di congelamento controllati, geochimica acquosa, monitoraggio del gas e caratterizzazione minerale per sviluppare un framework basato sul processo per la comprensione quando il congelamento promuove il rilascio del carbonio, lo stoccaggio del carbonio, o entrambi. Descrizione del lavoro
• Guidare ed eseguire esperimenti di laboratorio criogenici controllati utilizzando sistemi di reattore di congelamento e di scongelamento personalizzati.
• Misurare e interpretare i dati geochimici liquidi e gas utilizzando una varietà di strumentazione analitica (ad esempio, analizzatori di gas, HPIC, ICP-OES, UVVis-Spectroscopia, Titolazione potenzialemetrica).
• Recuperare e caratterizzare i minerali carbonati formati durante il congelamento utilizzando tecnica mineralogica e microscopica.
• Sviluppare e parametrizzare un framework cinetico predittivo utilizzando misurazioni geochimiche risolte nel tempo.
• sintetizzare i dati sperimentali e diffondere i risultati attraverso manoscritti scientifici.
• Presenta la tua ricerca a conferenze e workshop internazionali.
• Collabora a stretto contatto con il Principal Investigator, un ricercatore post-dottorato e altri membri del gruppo, contribuendo a una cultura di gruppo solidale e comunicativa. Profilo Stiamo cercando un candidato curioso, attento e motivato dalla ricerca sperimentale. Ti piace lavorare con sistemi geochimici complessi e sono entusiasti dalla sfida di sviluppare nuovi metodi e dataset.
• Laurea MSc in geochimica, scienze della terra, chimica ambientale, chimica, o una disciplina strettamente correlata.
• Un forte interesse o sfondo in geochimica a bassa temperatura, interazioni con l'acqua-rock, formazione minerale, carbonato e chimica acquosa redox, scienza della criosfera, o campi correlati.
• Motivazione per il lavoro di laboratorio pratico e la risoluzione dei problemi sperimentali.
• Eccellente analitica e problem solving competenze, tra cui la capacità di lavorare con attenzione con dati chimici quantitativi.
• Creatività, resilienza e indipendenza quando si lavora a domande di ricerca esplorativa.
• Capacità di lavorare sia indipendentemente che come parte di un team collaborativo.
• Ottimo parlato e scritto inglese. L'esperienza con la modellazione reattiva-trasporto/geochimica è utile ma non richiesto. Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Un ambiente di ricerca collaborativo: si unirà a un gruppo di ricerca entusiasta, inclusivo e altamente collaborativo dove la ricerca di alta qualità, la discussione aperta e il pensiero scientifico creativo sono fortemente apprezzati. Potrai beneficiare di un ambiente dipartimentale dinamico con ampia competenza, eccellenti infrastrutture di ricerca e opportunità di scambio interdisciplinare.
• Mentorialità e sviluppo di carriera: Riceverai una mentorship diretta dai membri PI e senior del gruppo insieme al supporto nello sviluppo delle tue competenze nel design sperimentale, nell'interpretazione dei dati, nella scrittura scientifica e nello sviluppo del framework accademico. Parteciperai alla più ampia comunità accademica attraverso pubblicazioni e presentazioni a conferenc scientifico
